📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that when Terence Young, the director of Dr. No, needed a suit for Sean Connery to wear for his debut as James Bond, he took him to see his personal Savile Row tailor, Anthony Sinclair.

Sources indicate that “Connery’s suits were considered relatively contemporary, because Anthony always had a very soft shoulder on his suits,” explains Elliot Mason, the director of business at Anthony Sinclair, which is no longer located on Savile Row, but still makes classic British suiting. “Anthony liked to nip in the waist, so it gave that real hourglass silhouette to the suit, which really is quite timeless. And as was the trend at the time, the Connery suits all had a relatively high rise, double-pleated with English forward pleats, and most of his trousers had Daks button-tab adjusters on the side.”.

Industry observers note that opting to dress James Bond in a Savile Row suit might seem like a no-brainer in hindsight, but the decision—and the cut of the suits themselves—still resonates more than 60 years later. Sinclair would make all of Connery’s suits during his nine-year run as James Bond, and his blend of classic British tailoring and of-the-moment influences would create a template for every Bond to come. With Robert Pattinson—a Dior ambassador and a guy with a reputation for adventurous style—chosen to take up the mantle in Bond 26, the question now becomes: what will he wear?

Tailor Anthony Sinclair fitting Sean Connery for one of the suits he wore in 1963’s From Russia With Love.

Sources indicate that ian Fleming, the author who created James Bond, spent a lot of time talking about what Agent 007 drank (Wolfschmidt Vodka) what he drove (Bentley convertibles, for the most part) and how he made his coffee (he was a dedicated pour-over guy), but, surprisingly, he never specified where the spy bought his clothes. As a result, for the last six decades, it’s been up to the directors and costume designers of the 25 previous films to create a newly introduced look for every successive Bond. In the Connery and Moore eras it was Savile Row suits. Timothy Dalton’s Bond wore Paul Smith. Brosnan was a bespoke Brioni guy, as was Daniel Craig, who also brought Tom Ford into the mix. At 6’1” to Craig’s 5’10”, with a leaner build, and a long track record of fashion-forward dressing, Pattinson has everything needed to reinvent Bond once again.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m pretty sure we’re going to see something quite different from Pattinson's Bond,” says Matt Spaiser, the tailoring obsessive behind BondSuits.com and the author of From Tailors with Love: An Evolution of Menswear Through the Bond Films. “Pattinson is a different kind of actor, and he’s going to wear something that moves differently. Plus, he’s 18 years younger than Daniel Craig.”.

Industry observers note that the actor playing Bond has a major influence on how he dresses—Daniel Craig, an adventurous dresser himself, was very hands-on with the wardrobe in his films—but Pattinson’s ongoing contract with Dior could also factor in. “Some of his Dior looks look somewhat like James Bond—he wears a great tuxedo—but I don’t think it’s going to tell us what he’s going to wear as James Bond,” Spaiser notes. “He’s worn suits from other brands in other roles—like in Tenet, he wasn’t wearing a Dior suit—so I don’t think he's necessarily obligated to be wearing Dior as James Bond.”.

Daniel Craig, seen here in 2019 with then-Prince Charles on the set of No Time to Die, mainly sported sharp Tom Ford suiting in his later Bond films.

Another important factor that contributes to a fresh Bond’s look is what’s happening in fashion whenever the film eventually gets made. “One thing that we've seen throughout most of the Bond eras is that he dresses in suits that are fairly traditional, but there's always some nod to the era that they’re in,” says Spaiser. “Sometimes they lean a little more into fashion, like when Roger Moore was wearing flares. That was something that I think they couldn't avoid without making Bond look too old-fashioned at the time.”.

According to recent reports, tone also plays an vital role, and historically has ping-ponged between serious (Connery, Dalton, Craig) and more campy (Moore, Brosnan), but with Denis Villeneuve, the auteur behind Sicario, Blade Runner: 2049, and Dune in the director’s chair, the smart money isn’t on hovercraft gondolas and punny Bond girl names. A darker, more atmospheric milieu could make for an interesting complement to Pattinson’s taste for high-fashion.

It has been revealed that if Mason were dressing Pattinson for the role, he says, he’d take a lead from his clientele, many of whom, like Bond, are well-heeled Londoners with a taste for expensive sports cars and well mixed cocktails. “The majority of our customers are reasonably conservative, and when it comes to fit, they’re sensitive to current trends,” Mason notes. As such, he’d opt for longer jackets, both single- and double-breasted, that are fuller through the body, and straight-leg pleated trousers. “It’s not that very, very slim fit that we'd seen for so many years, but it still needs to be refined,” he says. “I don’t think it would be appropriate to put him in wide-leg or baggy trousers. I just don't think it’s right for Bond.”.

Robert Pattinson, the latest 007, has been the face of Dior’s menswear for over a decade.

Given the intense scrutiny on every relaunch of the Bond franchise, and the tendency of fans to get worked up online over perceived mishandling of a beloved character, Pattinson, Villeneuve, and the film’s yet-to-be-announced costume designers have little room for error. Go too conservative and they’ll be accused of playing it safe; make Bond into a fashion guy, and they’ll incur the wrath of the traditionalists.

Sources indicate that “He needs to look current, but also timeless,” Spaiser says. “It’s a hard balance to find.”.

  • The fast food chain just released a limited-time Holiday Box complete with retro packaging, collectible knit hats, and a choice of some familiar menu favorites.
  • Available beginning November 16 at participating Wendy’s locations nationwide, the Holiday Box starts at $11.99 and includes your choice of a Dave’s Double or 10-piece crispy or spicy chicken nuggets, small fries, a small soft drink, and one collectible knit hat.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wendy’s is getting nostalgic this holiday season, and as someone who grew up eating in one of the chain’s iconic glass sunrooms, I’m particularly excited about this one.

The fast food chain just released a limited-time Holiday Box complete with retro packaging, collectible knit hats, and a choice of some familiar menu favorites. And of course, two latest peppermint-inspired Frosty desserts.

Obviously, I had to try everything for myself.

Available beginning November 16 at participating Wendy’s locations nationwide, the Holiday Box starts at $11.99 and includes your choice of a Dave’s Double or 10-piece crispy or spicy chicken nuggets, small fries, a small soft drink, and one collectible knit hat.

The packaging is designed to resemble Wendy’s old-school Solarium restaurants, complete with the recognizable glass-walled dining area that became a staple of the chain beginning in the 1980s.

And I have to admit, this one hit me right in the childhood memories.

Growing up, I remember going to Wendy’s with my mom and sitting in that yellow, glass-enclosed sunroom. Seeing the design recreated as a miniature holiday box immediately brought me back to those visits.

Each Holiday Box includes one of four collectible knit hats featuring a retro Wendy’s design: Frosty, Biggie, the classic Wendy’s logo, or the famous “Where’s the Beef?” slogan.

The hats come in sealed mystery bags, meaning you won’t know which one you’re getting until you open it.

Thankfully, I ended up with the blue Frosty beanie, which was exactly the design I was hoping for.

Had I opened the bag to find a hat with “Biggie” written across my forehead, though, I think we would’ve had a problem.

The Holiday Box is available for a limited time while supplies last, and customers can’t select which hat they receive.

Alongside the Holiday Box, Wendy’s is introducing two limited-time desserts: the Peppermint Frosty Swirl and Peppermint Brownie Frosty Fusion.

Both are available with either a vanilla or chocolate Frosty base, so I decided to try one of each.

This was easily my favorite of the two.

The Peppermint Brownie Frosty Fusion combines Wendy’s classic Frosty with peppermint sauce and brownie pieces, creating a dessert that feels especially appropriate for the holiday season.

I went with the vanilla base, and I absolutely loved it.

Recent findings suggest that the peppermint flavor was strong and immediately reminded me of a candy cane or a York Peppermint Pattie. It had that recognizable minty sweetness I look for in a holiday dessert, without getting lost in the vanilla Frosty.

According to recent reports, the brownie pieces were another highlight, adding a nice texture and a layer of chocolate flavor to the mix. I particularly liked how the chocolate complemented the peppermint rather than competing with it.

For me, this is exactly what a seasonal Frosty should taste like. It’s festive, flavorful, and different enough from the regular menu to make it worth trying.

For my second dessert, I went with the chocolate Peppermint Frosty Swirl, which combines Wendy’s classic Chocolate Frosty with peppermint sauce.

My biggest piece of advice is to give this one a good stir before digging in.

It has been revealed that when I first tried it, most of the peppermint syrup was concentrated toward the top of the dessert. Mixing everything together helped distribute the flavor more evenly throughout the Frosty.

Once I did that, I really enjoyed it.

The combination of chocolate and peppermint works well, although I didn’t find the mint flavor nearly as strong as it was in the vanilla Brownie Frosty Fusion.

Recent findings suggest that still, I’m happy to report that Wendy’s peppermint sauce works with both Frosty flavors. If you prefer a more straightforward chocolate-mint combination without brownie pieces, this is a solid option.

Personally, though, I’d go back for the Fusion.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that we’ve all been there: someone coughing on the subway immediately makes you jump, or you hear a friend you just sat next to at dinner has come down with a cold, and suddenly you’re overdosing on vitamin C.
  • According to recent reports, there are classic tricks like upping your vitamin C intake, washing your hands frequently, and drinking hot liquids like soup and tea, but what about the extreme hacks that hit the SOS button on your immune system—those under-the-radar, witchcraft-adjacent tricks?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here at Harper’s Bazaar, we are game to try anything and everything in the wellness world—from daily digestion walks to a $500 full-body assessment, and even supplements to boost ferritin levels—to stay healthy. But, like anyone else, we’re always hunting for newly introduced ways to avoid getting sick.

Industry observers note that we’ve all been there: someone coughing on the subway immediately makes you jump, or you hear a friend you just sat next to at dinner has come down with a cold, and suddenly you’re overdosing on vitamin C. Warding off a cold or viral sickness is not always possible—especially once cold and flu season rolls around.

According to recent reports, there are classic tricks like upping your vitamin C intake, washing your hands frequently, and drinking hot liquids like soup and tea, but what about the extreme hacks that hit the SOS button on your immune system—those under-the-radar, witchcraft-adjacent tricks? We have tried almost every tip and trick in the book—some work like a charm, and others are all hype and anecdotes—but ahead are the 14 hacks our editors swear by for staying healthy this cold season—and beyond.

“Tongue scraping has changed my life. Not only does it make your mouth feel much cleaner and support overall oral health, but I swear that since I started scraping religiously a few years back, I've been sick WAY less often. And I have a toddler! In daycare! My theory is that it scrapes away bacteria before it has a chance to settle in your throat—but who knows? No matter what the science states, there are only upsides—fresher breath, better teeth, and the satisfaction of seeing all that gunk removed." —Jenna Rosenstein, beauty director.

“As an out-and-proud hypochondriac, I have a long laundry list of cold-fighting hacks. The most vital is washing my hands frequently (as soon as I arrive somewhere latest, after taking the subway, after touching a public surface, etc.) and avoiding touching my face. I keep a compact hand sanitizer in every purse I own in case of emergency!” — Olivia Alchek, senior designer.

“I consider a good night's sleep a cure-all for just about anything, including incoming sickness. Not only does adequate rest help your body fight off infection by way of antibody and immune cell production, but it just makes you feel better in general, which is all you want when you're feeling borderline sick.” —Tiffany Dodson Davis, beauty commerce editor.

Recent findings suggest that “Most of my heavy-hitting cold fighters are from Europe (they’re just exponentially better over there), but when it comes to sick solutions stateside, I always have Wellness Formula stocked in my house. I don’t know what sorcery is in these pills, but once I take this, whether it’s when a sniffle or tickle in my throat comes up, or if I am already deep into a cold, I feel better the next day. The pills contain all the gold-standard immunity ingredients: elderberry, zinc, propolis, echinacea, and vitamins C and D, plus vitamins and minerals that are good to take generally, like selenium, calcium, and vitamin A. The only downside is a pungent aftertaste (likely from the garlic bulb in the formula), and the daily dose is 6 pills, which is more than many can handle. If you don’t like pills, there’s a liquid version that works just as well, but I prefer the pills for when I travel.” —Katie Intner, beauty market and commerce editor.

According to recent reports, “Even in the post-COVID era, I still wear K-N95 masks on public transit. It’s the most successful way to avoid unwanted germs. Thinking about thousands of Fresh Yorkers on a crowded subway, sniffling in the winter months—I’ll never go back to being mask-free again!” —OA.

Industry observers note that “As soon as I feel a scratchy throat coming on, I break out the Vicks. Slather it on and let it do its old-timey magic.” —Lillian Dondero, assistant managing editor.

“When people say to ‘flush out a cold,’ they typically mean drink lots of fluids, but I love dry brushing to get the lymphatic system moving and grooving to rid any toxins from the cold. I do it for two minutes before I shower, and I instantly feel my lymphatic system activated and more energized. Plus, it doubles as exfoliation, which is key during the winter months.” —KI.

In a recent development, “Throat Coat tea is my holy grail whenever I’m feeling under the weather. I love the subtle licorice flavor, and it’s incredibly soothing on an irritated throat. I always keep it stocked at home and reach for it at the first sign of a cold. Honestly, it’s so good that I even drink it when I’m not sick!” —Jackie Judd, executive assistant.

Sources indicate that “Whenever the thought ‘Oh, I think I might be getting a cold’ enters my brain, I immediately go to the pharmacy to pick up some Zicam. I don’t know if this is the official tagline, but in my head it is ‘stops a cold before you get it’ because IT. DOES! The trick is to buy the kind that goes up your nose—spray or swabs—and be diligent; your symptoms won't progress, and then they'll go away completely. It's magic!” —Laia Garcia-Furtado, deputy culture director.

“A shot before work is my way of staying healthy! My fridge is always stocked with Greenhouse Juice Co. dispensers because I truly can never live without them. A quick shot to kickstart my day is a great immunity boost, and the spice is a great bonus, as it always helps wake me up.” —Claudia Cruz, deputy visual director.

“Liquid echinacea everywhere! I keep it in my bag and squeeze it into everything—even my coffee.” —Lynette Nylander, executive digital director.

“I love Cymbiotika’s liposomal technology because the lipid base makes it more easily absorbed into the bloodstream and is therefore more effective. I always use these vitamin C packets when I feel a cold coming on or know I will be low on sleep, like while traveling, because they truly boost my immunity and taste like a creamsicle. Life is hard enough! I want a supplement that works and tastes good.

I will often couple the Cymbiotika vitamin C with a packet of the Armra Colostrum, which protects and boosts immunity.” —KI.

“When I’m already experiencing cold symptoms? Downing a spoonful of honey—both anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial—with a squeeze of lemon does wonders for my itchy throat or stubborn cough." —TDD.

According to recent reports, “My most homeopathic tip whenever I start to feel symptoms is to eat raw garlic. Garlic contains a compound called allicin, which is released when you crush, chop, or chew it. Allicin is known to have immune-boosting, antimicrobial, and antiviral properties that may shorten illness. Does it actually work? Who knows! But it doesn’t hurt to crush a little garlic in olive oil for dipping toast. It’s a harmless, delicious extra step in my sick day routine.” —OA.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that it’s all about the multi-purpose fragrance this week as search data highlights growing interest in fragrances that combine practical formats, occasion-led scents, and distinctive notes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Vogue Business Beauty Tracker, produced in collaboration with Spate, tracks the top five brands, trends and ingredients that are driving the most significant positive change in year-on-year growth that have also demonstrated consistent upward growth historically. Each week, we’ll spotlight a different beauty category and the top five beauty hashtags on TikTok.

It has been revealed that it’s all about the multi-purpose fragrance this week as search data highlights growing interest in fragrances that combine practical formats, occasion-led scents, and distinctive notes. Searches for Chanel’s Coco Mademoiselle Fragrance Primer reflect demand for prep products that extend a scent’s wear, projection, and hold on the skin. Travel fragrance shows continued interest in travel-size versions of full-size scents. Meanwhile, wedding fragrance reflects demand for a dedicated signature scent for the big day, and white floral perfume highlights interest in scents built around blossoms such as jasmine, gardenia, and tuberose, while pineapple fragrance signals demand for bright, tropical fruit notes.

Recent findings suggest that for fragrance brands, there is growing interest in concept-driven scents, heritage expertise, and affordable fragrance lines. Lore fragrances inspire specific memories, moods, and places, while Toskovat, an independent niche perfume house from Romania, stands out for composing each scent as a “bottled memory”, or extrait de mémoire. Shiseido reflects interest in the Japanese house’s heritage fragrances, with searches focused on Zen. Ranger Station, based in Nashville, draws on music culture and American landscapes for its unisex, artisan-style scents. Finally, Old Navy points to demand for affordable fragrance through Old Navy Beauty Co., its line of hair and body mists, lotions, and body washes, which expanded in August 2026.

It’s all about hair and nail maintenance on TikTok this week.

#KTipHairExtension reflects interest in semi-permanent extensions, with stylists showing how individual strands are bonded to natural hair using keratin tips. #CurlyHairGel and #CurlyHairVolume highlight interest in curly hair styling, from gels that keep curls defined, hydrated, and frizz-free to techniques that build lift and fullness at the root. #HolidayEyeMakeup points to interest in festive, party-ready eye looks, with tutorials circulating ahead of the winter holidays. Meanwhile, #CuticleRemover centers on at-home nail care, with videos demonstrating how to use Sally Hansen’s Instant Cuticle Remover.

According to recent reports, at-home application and retro, graphic designs are among this month’s biggest nail trends. Searches for solid gel polish are on the rise, reflecting demand for a thicker, pot-based gel formula designed for more controlled application, while press-on sets remain popular for their reusability. White chrome powder, which creates a pearly, mirror-like finish when buffed over gel polish, is trending in time for the winter months, as well as geometric nail designs for their clean lines and shapes. Meanwhile, vintage nail polishes, including Urban Decay’s discontinued metallic foil shades, reinforce consumer interest in discontinued products that allow for a nostalgic aesthetic.

For nail brands, DIY manicure solutions, art-driven designs, and everyday nail tools are proving a success. The rise of Cyprus-based brand Doonails reflects demand for do-it-yourself manicure and pedicure products designed to deliver salon-quality results. Never Have I Ever reflects demand for reusable press-on nails featuring licensed artwork from independent artists and cultural icons, while Double Rhythm underscores interest in accessible soak-off gel polishes and nail art supplies. Heyhae offers sun-cured gel nail strips that harden naturally in sunlight without requiring a traditional UV or LED lamp, and Diamond Cosmetics signals continued interest in accessible nail products that offer variety and affordability.

In a recent development, hair how-to content is ever-growing on TikTok, with creators twisting small sections of coily hair into a #coiltwist or #CurlsWithStraightener tutorials doing the rounds. Meanwhile, the rise in videos showing off #DarkBalayage points to demand for soft, dimensional color finishes on brunette and black hair, which offers a subtle look that minimizes root visibility. There’s also rising demand for lip stains that provide #AllDayLipColor, while #TestingMakeup content demonstrates creators trying out upcoming viral products in their full-face routines, sharing verdicts as they go.

The makeup products consumers are searching for the most are those combining precise application, long wear, and shimmering finishes. Tools such as winged eyeliner stamps take the stress and guesswork out of creating a sharp, even cat-eye look, while creamy lip liners offer buildable definition through soft, blendable formulas. Gripping primers and longwear lipsticks also reflect demand for staying power, from tacky primers that give makeup a sticky base to lip formulas designed to resist fading and transfer. Meanwhile, the rise of rose gold eyeshadow highlights interest in pink-toned metallic shades that add dimension to eye looks.

It has been revealed that when it comes to makeup brands, lasting interest in Burberry Beauty signals the strength of luxury cosmetics from established fashion houses, especially foundations. Nude by Nature highlights demand for makeup powered by natural Australian botanicals. Beauty Creations, a Latina-founded brand, stands out for high-pigment formulas, frequent limited-edition collections, and pop culture partnerships. Sculpted by Aimee, founded by makeup artist Aimee Connolly, reflects interest in multitasking, skin-first products that simplify daily routines. Finally, KeyYou points to demand for lash extension kits and cluster lashes designed for self-application.

It has been revealed that there’s a demand for the nostalgic on TikTok, with the #ThrowBackBeauty hashtag showing creators recreating and reviewing makeup, hair, and fashion looks from past decades. Over on #PerfumeTok, the fragrance community is reviewing, ranking, and recommending scents, while #BlackFridayBeautyDeals points to anticipation ahead of TikTok Shop’s official Black Friday campaign. Meanwhile, #FalseLashesTutorial reflects demand for step-by-step guidance on applying false lashes, and #ServerHairInspo highlights low-maintenance hairstyles built to last throughout the work shift — fueled by the viral “server hair theory” that certain styles can earn servers higher tips.

Industry observers note that skincare products that combine regenerative ingredients, targeted application, and everyday hydration are on the rise in search. Fresh PDRN formats — creams, face masks, and eye patches — reinforce interest in the ingredient, which is associated with cellular repair and a stronger skin barrier, as well as its use in targeted treatments like the Abib PDRN Retinal Eye Patch. Increased searches for hyaluronic acid face lotion reflects demand for deep hydration in everyday skincare, while liquid pimple patches highlight interest in subtle formulas that directly target blemishes and dry into an invisible film.

In a recent development, skincare consumers are particularly intrigued in brands combining clinical-grade formulas, advanced delivery technologies, and everyday sun protection. Magic Molecule reflects continued demand for hypochlorous acid, offering a multi-purpose, FDA-cleared spray for everyday skincare. KRX Aesthetics and Meditherapy, both South Korean brands, are known for their professional skin treatments adapted for at-home use. Radical Skincare stands out for its performance-driven anti-aging formulas, powered by its proprietary Trylacel delivery technology. Finally, Invisible Zinc reflects demand for mineral-based sunscreens that use zinc oxide as the primary ingredient instead of chemical UV filters.

According to recent reports, over on TikTok, #DolphinSkin reflects interest in ultra-glossy, smooth, and luminous skin, specifically on the body. #GreenChromeNails and #ColorLashes highlight bold approaches to color, from mirror-like metallic manicures in shades of green to multi-colored lash looks. Content featuring #TTSKbeauty, or TikTok Shop K-beauty, shows the platform’s growing role in K-beauty product discovery. Meanwhile, the rise of #JasmineFragrance is driven by Chun Breeze Xian Jasmine, a Chinese fragrance that creators compare to the jasmine tea scent of tea house chains Molly Tea and Heytea.

Industry observers note that in haircare, products that combine scalp support, deep nourishment, and targeted cleansing are trending in search. Peptide hair serums cater to those seeking lightweight formulas that support fuller-looking hair, with searches associated primarily with The Ordinary’s Multi-Peptide Serum for Hair Density, while hair thinning serums points to a broader focus on density and scalpcare. Rice water hair spray highlights interest in a convenient leave-in format for an ingredient valued for adding strength and shine. Cholesterol hair treatment reflects demand for rich, deep-conditioning masks that restore moisture and softness, and chlorine removal shampoo signals demand for clarifying formulas that remove chlorine build-up post-swim.

When it comes to brands, the rise of K-beauty player Lilyeve reflects demand for daily scalpcare, with searches led by its Scalp Turn Cica PDRN Brush Ampoule, a cooling leave-in treatment applied through a built-in brush head. Demand for Honeyque products highlights interest in salon-grade Japanese haircare designed to repair dry, damaged and frizzy hair, while Chāmpo stands out for blending ayurvedic principles with modern trichology, particularly through its hair serum. Bare Anatomy underscores continued demand for science-backed, dermatologically tested haircare, from anti-dandruff shampoo to a roll-on scalp serum. Finally, Brickell Men’s Products reflects interest in natural grooming formulated specifically for men.

According to recent reports, beyond traditional beauty content, #MakeupGame on TikTok reflects the growing overlap between beauty and gaming, with posts centered around Makeup Mania, a Roblox game where players compete through makeup and fashion looks. #HowToSilkPress and #4CWashDay highlight continued demand for textured hair education, from step-by-step silk press tutorials to wash day routines tailored to tightly coiled 4C hair. The #GlitterAcrylic hashtag points to interest in sparkling, statement acrylic nail sets, while #EczemaPatch highlights the hydrocolloid format popularized by pimple patches expanding to eczema-prone skin.

Recent findings suggest that in the wellness world, there’s growing interest in specialized nutrition and brands that prioritize convenience and targeted health benefits. Pure Genius Protein reflects demand for portable, high-protein formats, with ready-to-drink shots providing 23 grams of protein per serving. Sisel highlights a broad approach to wellness through dietary supplements and functional beverages, while Toplux Nutrition emphasizes science-backed supplements at affordable prices. Wip stands out for its nicotine-free caffeine pouches, offering a convenient format for an energy boost. Finally, Triquetra Health reflects interest in gut and metabolic wellness, with searches focused on its GLP-Pro probiotic and postbiotic supplement. Collectively, these brands span everyday protein intake, energy support, and targeted nutritional supplementation.

In the midst of October, #HalloweenHairClips are trending on TikTok, reflecting interest in festive, spooky hair accessories — particularly horror-themed claw clips and seasonal designs. Meanwhile, the rise of #LadybugMakeup highlights whimsical, insect-inspired makeup looks also tailored to spooky season. Across manicure content, #UglyNails are performing well, as more unconventional and unusual nail designs gain traction for allowing artistic expression, while #PinkCateyeNails reflects interest in light-reflecting cateye designs in shades of pink. The #CoilyCurly hashtag celebrates natural hair textures between curly and coily, with content focused on haircare tips and styling.

Sources indicate that products that combine hydration, targeted care and sensory experiences are ruling the bodycare category. Hydrating body mists meet demand for lightweight, water-like moisturizers that deliver lotion-level hydration, while anti-sweat hand creams offer targeted solutions for managing perspiration on the hands. Growing demand for hand mists suggest interest in convenient, fragrant formats that refresh and sanitize on the go, while niacinamide body wash is an example of products designed to support the skin’s moisture barrier. Finally, strawberry body scrub reflects demand for fruit-inspired bodycare that combines exfoliation with appealing scents and ingredients.

Across bodycare brands, there’s growing interest in those offering specialized and efficient approaches to personal care and grooming. Carpe reflects demand for clinical-strength sweat and odor control, while Hanni highlights simplified bodycare through “skip-step” essentials, with a particular rise in searches for its Splash Salve in-shower body balm. Proraso stands out for its Italian men’s grooming heritage. Estée Lauder has evolved its fragrance range by incorporating bodycare into its iconic scent collections, as searches for its Beautiful Perfumed Body Powder grow. Meanwhile, Prequel reflects interest in dermatologist-developed, science-backed skincare centered on skin barrier health.

Sources indicate that this week on TikTok, the #DiscountMakeup hashtag is flooded with shoppers unexpectedly discovering Jeffree Star Cosmetics products at Dollar Tree. Meanwhile, content around #PerfumeMists is focused on reviews and recommendations of lightweight, refreshing fragrance formats. #TattooLipLiner content is also on the rise, featuring ink-like liners, peel-off stains, and semi-permanent lip treatments for long-lasting lip definition. #GlowyMakeupRoutine points to interest in luminous, radiant makeup looks and routines, while #FeatheredHair highlights interest in the ’70s voluminous, heavily layered hair look. Together, these trends highlight how beauty content is increasingly shaped by product discovery, makeup routines and nostalgic aesthetics.

There’s growing interest in fragrance trends that combine personalization, identity, and convenience. Alcohol-free fragrances, for example, reflect demand for alternative formulations to traditional perfumes, while custom perfumes point to interest in personalized scents tailored to individual preferences. The rise of masculine fragrances suggests that scent is increasingly functioning as an identity marker for male and female consumers alike, while gothic perfume reflects demand for darker and more mysterious aromatic profiles that evoke the romantic and atmospheric elements of the goth aesthetic. Finally, travel fragrances, the portable and convenient scent formats designed to make fragrance easier to pack and use on the go, are also trending.

According to recent reports, this month, there’s particular interest in fragrance brands offering distinctive approaches to scent. Lore’s emotive, transportive fragrances translate specific moods and places into immersive scent experiences, while MCM Fragrance and Miu Miu highlight growing interest in luxury scents that extend recognizable fashion identities into fragrance, with searches for the latter mainly associated with Miutine and its youthful fragrance identity. Ranger Station stands out for its bold, high-concentration, nature-inspired scents, while Maison d’Etto offers perfumes rooted in equestrian influence, contemporary art and architecture. These brands highlight growing consumer interest in fragrance that goes beyond scent itself, offering distinctive stories, identities and sensory experiences.

It has been revealed that as we enter October season, #SpookyNailArt is trending on TikTok, reflecting interest in Halloween-inspired nail designs based on playful motifs. Meanwhile, growing interest in the #MakeupColorTheory reinforces the rise of consumers learning about the hues that enhance their features. #ConcertHair highlights demand for hairstyles that are durable, creative and highly accessorized, specifically designed to last throughout a concert, while the #RomanticUpdo reflects interest in soft, feminine hairstyles and intentionally undone styles. #CologneHaul demonstrates interest in discovering and showcasing fragrance purchases and collections.

Sources indicate that when it comes to nails, there’s a growing interest in trends that combine precision, personalization, and visually distinct finishes. The Italian manicure, which creates the appearance of longer slender nails, reflects demand for more precise techniques, while nail art pens and letters on nails point to interest in customized designs and intricate details. The rise of glass nail polish highlights a preference for glossy, translucent finishes, and vibrant nails reflect demand for bold, eye-catching colors.

According to recent reports, among this month’s trending nail brands, there’s a clear preference for distinct approaches to at-home manicures. Reusable, press-on nail line Never Have I Ever incorporates licensed artwork from independent artists and cultural icons into nail designs, while Double Rhythm reinforces interest in accessible, soak-off gel polishes and nail art supplies for DIY and salon-style looks. IPolish stands out for its digital color-changing press-on nails, allowing owners to switch between hundreds of shades using a smartphone and activation wand. Heyhae offers sun-cured gel nail strips that harden naturally in sunlight without requiring a traditional UV or LED lamp, while Sparkle & Co. specializes in DIY dip powders with unique glitters, foils, flakes, glow-in-the-dark, and color-changing effects.

TikTok is seeing an influx of content featuring #BumperBangs, reflecting interest in vintage 1940s and ’50s fringe styles consisting of a bold, rounded shape. Meanwhile, the rise of #CurlyHairBride highlights demand for bridal hair inspiration that embraces natural curls and textured styles. #WigsOnTikTok shows the growing role of TikTok in discovering, styling, and showcasing wigs. #UltaFragrance and #SephoraBeautyAdvisor highlight interest in beauty advisors sharing recommendations, product expertise and customer interactions at retailers Ulta and Sephora. Together, these hashtags highlight interest in vintage looks, occasion-specific styling, and behind-the-scenes beauty retail experiences.

Sources indicate that there’s a growing interest in makeup products that combine ease of use, enhanced appearance, and convenient beauty benefits, according to monthly search data. Growth in creamy lip liners points to demand for smooth, easy-to-apply products that shape and define the lips, while lip volumizers help create the appearance of fuller, smoother lips without invasive treatments. Rose gold eyeshadow is also trending, driven by demand for warm, luminous shades. Gripping primer, which is a gel-based product with a tacky finish to hold your makeup in place, reflects interest in creating durable makeup looks that last throughout the day. The rise of SPF face powder reveals interest in facial sun protection beyond conventional sunscreens, with multifunctional products that both protect and control shine.

Across makeup brands, those offering distinctive products spanning various price points are performing particularly well. Hung Vanngo Beauty reflects demand for makeup artist expertise, while Burberry Beauty signals continued interest in luxury cosmetics from established fashion houses. C-beauty brand Cheeryep and Sleek Makeup highlight demand for vibrant, high-pigment makeup and innovative finishes. Maven Beauty, Fashion Nova’s makeup brand, suggests growing demand for affordable beauty options.

According to recent reports, on TikTok, #UVHairExtensions are gaining traction, reflecting interest in innovative UV and LED hair extension techniques offering fast application, while #BrownRedHair highlights demand for rich, warm hair color combinations of brown, red, copper, and mahogany tones. Manicurist content featuring #PracticeNails shows past designs and their training progress, while #CottagecoreNails spotlights whimsical, nature-inspired manicures influenced by cottagecore aesthetics. The rise of #BridesmaidsMakeup reflects growing demand for beauty inspiration tailored to bridesmaids and wedding looks.

Sources indicate that in skincare, monthly interest in products and treatments that combine targeted skin health benefits with gentle, barrier-supporting ingredients and advanced technologies is rising. Silicone-free sunscreen and its lightweight, ingredient-conscious sun protection is trending, while the retinol sandwich method, where retinol is layered between moisturizer to reduce the risk of irritation, is gaining traction among those looking to safely introduce retinol into their routines. There is continued demand for hyaluronic acid face lotions offering convenient, hydrating properties that support moisture retention and skin plumpness, while ceramide toners are designed to strengthen and maintain the skin barrier. Interest in high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) treatments highlights demand for advanced, non-invasive aesthetic treatments focused on skin tightening and rejuvenation.

According to recent reports, for brands, those offering science-backed and targeted skincare solutions are trending. Elm Biosciences, which develops clinical skincare focused on healthy aging and cellular-level care, is gaining traction, while Magic Molecule offers hypochlorous acid solutions that cleanse, reduce inflammation and support skin healing. The rise of TropicSport signals demand for high-performance sun protection during active lifestyles. NewGel+ reflects interest in specialized scarcare and skin repair. The Body Shop, particularly its Drops of Youth line, highlights demand for products targeting early signs of aging while supporting skin resilience against daily environmental stressors.

Industry observers note that on TikTok, #SheinMakeupHaul is trending, reflective of the growing interest in discovering and sharing affordable makeup products through beauty hauls. #BestHairOils reveals how more consumers are comparing different hair oils and seeking product recommendations. #BakedBlush features content spotlighting new blush rolls out and shades comparisons through product swatches and reviews. #TinselBraids and #CakeNails highlight playful approaches to self-expression through decorative hairstyles and creative nail designs, with consumers exploring visually distinctive looks.

This month’s search data highlights growing interest in haircare products that combine targeted follicle growth with plant-based ingredients. Popular hair serums range from including specific active ingredients, with searches for redensyl and peptide serums that help reduce shedding by supporting follicle health and improving fullness, to concern-specific searches such as hair thinning serum. Rice water hairspray highlights demand for convenient, multifunctional products that can strengthen strands, add shine and reduce frizz, while plant-based shampoos reflect growing interest in products made primarily with vegan and botanical ingredients.

When it comes to haircare brands, those offering performance-driven, science-backed and premium solutions, in particular, are trending. Labo-H reflects demand for Korean scalpcare and hair loss prevention, while UltraSwim highlights interest in cleansing products designed to remove chlorine, chemical odors, and mineral buildup from hair. Bare Anatomy signals demand for science-backed haircare, addressing specific concerns such as shedding, dandruff, frizz, and damage, while Bvlgari Beauty reflects interest in luxury products combining cleansing and scalpcare with the brand’s signature scents. Meanwhile, Iso Beauty highlights growing interest in solutions that deliver salon-quality results at home.

According to recent reports, over on TikTok, #BabyShowerMakeup reflects interest in soft glam makeup looks tailored specifically for mothers and guests attending baby showers, while #MarchMakeup shows makeup looks based on the birthday month. #QuickCurls highlights demand for fast and easy hairstyling techniques for curly hair, while #LakeHair reflects interest in solutions to avoid or untangle the messy, textured, and sometimes dry or mineral-coated hair associated with freshwater swimming. #AntioxidantSerum shows dermatologist content discussing skincare products centered around antioxidant benefits and protection from environmental stressors.

Across wellness, monthly search data highlights growing interest in products that combine targeted benefits, convenience, and ease of use. Dopamine patches, for example, reflect demand for wearable solutions associated with mood and focus support, while acupressure wristbands reveal interest in convenient solutions for managing and preventing nausea, particularly concerning travel and motion sickness. Screenless fitness trackers demonstrate growing demand for minimalist wearable technology that passively monitors health and activity data without the distraction of a screen. Men’s fertility supplements signal interest in targeted nutritional support for male reproductive health, while liquid zinc supplements highlight demand for convenient ways to prevent or address zinc deficiency and support immune health.

In a recent development, for brands, there’s growing interest in those offering targeted, convenient, and science-backed wellness solutions. Pure Genius Protein reflects demand for portable, easy-to-consume protein products, while Artemis Tea highlights interest in organic herbal teas and wellness blends rooted in traditional herbalism. Nancy’s Probiotic signals demand for organic cultured foods and probiotic-focused nutrition, while EFX Sports reflects interest in performance supplements such as Kre-Alkalyn creatine, designed to support strength and recovery. The rise of Sparkle Wellness relates to continued interest in collagen supplements targeting skin, hair, nails, and overall vitality.

Over on TikTok, the growing traction for #BridalUpdoStyle reflects interest in polished, occasion-ready hairstyles for weddings and special events. #FauxBrows and #HowToSelfTan highlight different approaches to enhancing everyday beauty, from creating realistic, hair-like brow strokes to achieving an even, natural-looking tan at home. #MakeupPR reflects the influencer culture around receiving and unboxing gifted beauty products, as well as creators sharing their experiences with brands. #MakeupOver35 highlights growing interest in makeup techniques and product recommendations tailored to women over the age of 35.

Recent findings suggest that in the bodycare space, current search trends highlight growing interest in products that combine targeted benefits and convenience with sensory appeal. Alpha hydroxy (AHA) body lotions and hand exfoliators reflect demand for exfoliating and smoothing products that help remove dead skin cells, dirt, and dry patches. Grape soap highlights playful, fruit-inspired formats that combine functionality with novelty and aesthetics. Epsom salt lotions reflect interest in convenient options for muscle relief and recovery, while kojic acid lotions signal demand for targeted brightening and uneven skin tone care.

In a recent development, as for bodycare brands, those offering targeted, skin-friendly solutions are gaining traction. QV Skincare reflects demand for sensitive skin and barrier-supportive care, while Naked Bee highlights interest in affordable, natural bodycare options incorporating ingredients such as honey, beeswax, and oatmeal. Derman points to demand for targeted antifungal treatments, and Curology reflects growing interest in dermatologist-designed solutions for body breakouts and rough texture. Meanwhile, Luna Daily highlights demand for pH-balanced, microbiome-friendly care for both the body and intimate areas. These brands reveal how the category is evolving through specialist treatments based on body area and skin concern, spanning natural-based products to dermatologist-designed solutions.

Over on TikTok, #VampNails reflect interest in bold, dramatic nail looks inspired by dark and vampy aesthetics. #RootRetouch and #GrayGrowOut highlight different approaches to managing hair color, from concealing visible roots to embracing the transition to natural gray. #HairVolumeHacks signals demand for accessible styling techniques that create fuller, more voluminous hair. #MakeupTrial reflects interest in testing and refining makeup looks ahead of weddings and special events.

This month’s search data highlights a shift toward more occasion-driven and emotionally evocative fragrance choices. The rise of wedding fragrances reflects growing interest in scents associated with meaningful celebrations and special occasions. Sport fragrances signal demand for fresh, energetic scents suited to active lifestyles and everyday wear, while sweet fragrances highlight continued preference for gourmand and indulgent scent profiles, with birthday cake perfume, for example, also offering a familiar scent evocative of childhood memories. Electric perfume, meanwhile, with searches mainly associated with the iconic Revlon fragrance from the 80s, Electric Youth, reflects the enduring appeal of discontinued scents that offer a latest form of nostalgia.

When it comes to brands, DefineMe Creative Studio highlights growing interest in fragrance rooted in pop culture, with collaborations such as Barbie connecting scent with recognizable characters and cultural identities. Lore reflects demand for emotive, transportive fragrances that translate specific moods and places into scent experiences. Miu Miu and MCM Fragrance highlight growing interest in luxury scents that extend a recognizable fashion identity into the perfume space, with Miu Miu searches mainly associated with the more youthful and feminine Miutine scent. The rise of Kopari, specifically its fragrance mists, reflects demand for lighter fragrance formats suited to everyday use.

On TikTok, #CreamEyeshadowSticks are trending, as demand rises for convenient, easy-to-apply makeup formats that allow consumers to create smooth, buildable eye looks with minimal effort. #ChunkyHighlights and #NailFoils reflect growing interest in creative beauty techniques that add dimension and visual impact to hair and nails. #UltaHairSalon reflects consumers’ and salon workers’ experiences with hair services in retail stores, highlighting a convenient way to access professional salon expertise. The continued interest in #DrySkinSolutions signals demand for targeted skincare solutions focused on relieving dryness and supporting skin hydration.

According to recent reports, there’s been a rise in search data for nail art pens, reflecting growing interest in personalized nail creativity that’s nostalgic and enables consumers to experiment with intricate and customized designs. Liquid tape reflects demand for manicure tools that simplify application while improving precision and creating cleaner, more professional-looking results. Glitter nail polish is another Y2K trend regaining momentum, with continued interest in bold, statement-making finishes that add a dose of playfulness to nail looks. The sustained demand for glass nail polish underscores the role of high-gloss translucent finishes as a more classic aesthetic. Meanwhile, celestial nails signal increasing enthusiasm for imaginative and artistic nail designs inspired by cosmic themes and metallic accents.

In a recent development, nars, which phased out its nail polish line, is trending in search data, reflecting the enduring appeal of discontinued beauty products when consumers maintain connections with iconic shades and search for color dupes still available on the market. Tonic Polish and Pure Ice, meanwhile, highlight growing interest in expressive nail finishes, such as multichromes, magnetics and holographics, as well as accessible trend-driven shades, glitters and metallics that keep manicures more unique. Beyond polish, Burt’s Bees highlights growing demand for nourishing nailcare solutions, such as cuticle creams that provide hydration while supporting dry and brittle nails. Diamond Cosmetics signals continued interest in accessible nail products that offer variety and affordability.

Industry observers note that on TikTok, #BrighteningEyeMasks reflect demand for targeted skincare solutions, with consumers using under-eye patches to depuff, hydrate, and reduce the appearance of dark circles. Content featuring #MakeupDisaster and #BadNailsCheck highlights the interest from consumers in beauty mishaps, from makeup products that fail to deliver expected results to manicure disasters and negative salon experiences. #SkincareRitual reflects interest in consistent, personalized skincare routines focused on daily maintenance. #NailTechDayInMyLife reflects interest in behind-the-scenes nail content, with consumers engaging with nail technicians’ routines, creative processes, and the realities of running a nail business. Together, these trends reflect growing consumer interest in authentic beauty experiences and personal routines.

Sources indicate that in the makeup space, monthly data highlights growing demand for innovative, personalized, and tech-driven cosmetics. Lipstick printers, associated primarily with YSL Beauty, reflect rising interest in tech-enabled beauty personalization, allowing consumers to create customized lip shades on-demand. Aloe lipstick offers hydrating, soothing properties with pH-reactive formulas that adapt to each wearer’s lips. Soft matte lipstick reflects interest in formulas that deliver a velvety, blurred matte finish without the dryness of traditional matte lipsticks, while terracotta lipstick highlights the popularity of warm, earthy shades that offer a transeasonal beauty look. Meanwhile, ginger mascara signals growing interest in softer, natural-looking eye makeup, with this shade offering a light brown to reddish tint that subtly enhances lashes.

It has been revealed that prestige Cosmetics is among this month’s trending makeup brands, reflecting continued demand for accessible, high-pigment products in a broad range of colors. Hung Vanngo Beauty signals sustained interest in makeup artist-founded brands that deliver professional-quality products based on their expertise. Details by Tati signals demand for creator-led beauty brands centered on luxury makeup tools and elevated application. Black Up is a brand tailored to those looking for inclusive makeup options, offering complexion products specifically developed to enhance deeper skin tones. The enduring appeal of Burberry Beauty, meanwhile, reinforces demand for combining premium formulations with sophisticated, fashion-inspired aesthetics.

Over on TikTok, #FrizzyHairHacks and #GrayHairCare reflect growing demand for targeted hair solutions, as more consumers seek practical techniques and specialized products to manage frizz, improve smoothness, and maintain the health and vibrancy of gray and silver hair. #GoldenHourMakeup highlights demand for warm, radiant beauty looks, from golden-toned eye makeup to sun-kissed complexions with natural luminosity. The rise of the #BlondeRoots hashtag reflects continued interest in blonde hair trends that embrace visible roots, like ghost roots. #FullFaceOfDollarTreeMakeup underscores engagement in affordable beauty experimentation, with consumers creating full-face looks using accessible products.

In the skincare space, there’s growing demand for targeted, science-led solutions. Pore mousse reflects interest in innovative K-beauty cleansing formats that deeply purify and refine the appearance of pores, while silicone scar sticks demonstrate demand for convenient scar care that supports scar recovery and improves the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles. Liquid pimple patches are still rising as the next-generation blemish treatment to combine targeted ingredient delivery with an invisible, flexible finish for everyday wear. Peptide eyelash serum reflects rising interest in peptide-powered formulas that strengthen lashes and promote a fuller, healthier appearance. Meanwhile, increased searches regarding retinoid dermatitis signals the heightened awareness of managing irritation associated with active skincare ingredients.

It has been revealed that when it comes to skincare brands, Elm Biosciences underscores growing interest in science-backed, clinically developed products, with a lab-to-patient approach focused on supporting long-term skin health and healthy aging. Caire Beauty reflects demand for hormone-aware skincare for women aged 40 to 65-plus, offering science-driven formulas designed to address the visible effects of perimenopause and menopause through advanced hydration and skin-rebuilding technologies.

In a recent development, love From Yours highlights the rise of AI-powered personalized skincare, using skin analysis and lifestyle data to create customized routines tailored to individual needs. Radical Skincare represents continued interest in clinical-strength anti-aging solutions that deliver restorative results while remaining suitable for sensitive and blemish-prone skin. Scarlett Whitening, an Indonesian brand, signals growing demand for accessible, ingredient-focused skincare that combines brightening, hydrating, and acne-targeting actives.

It has been revealed that on TikTok, #GlutenFreeMakeup reflects growing interest in inclusive beauty products that cater to ingredient-conscious consumers and specific lifestyle preferences. #FrenchTwistHairstyle and #ColorMelting reflect growing interest in elevated yet wearable hair looks, with consumers embracing timeless styling techniques alongside dimensional, natural-looking hair color trends. #CreamyEyeliner highlights demand for versatile eye makeup products that offer smooth application, rich pigmentation, and effortless wear. #MorningMakeupRoutine points to consumers seeking efficient, everyday beauty rituals and product recommendations that simplify their routines. Together, these trends reflect growing demand for beauty solutions that balance self-expression, convenience, and performance.

In the haircare space, there is growing interest in haircare solutions that combine convenience and science-backed ingredients alongside targeted treatments to support hair and scalp health. Convenience is a major factor, with waterless dry shampoo and 6-in-1 shampoo signaling the desire for multifunctional products that simplify hair care routines.

Industry observers note that caffeine hair serum highlights increasing interest in scalp-focused formulations designed to help strengthen hair, reduce shedding, and promote the appearance of fuller, healthier-looking hair. Exosome hair therapy underscores the growing popularity of advanced, science-driven hair restoration technologies, with consumers exploring treatments aimed at supporting scalp health, hair regeneration, and overall hair vitality. Finally, overnight hair serum reflects rising demand for treatments that work while users sleep, delivering deep hydration, nourishment, and repair to improve hair strength and smoothness by morning.

In a recent development, these trends can also been seen across the haircare brands spiking interest, with science and ingredients sitting at the forefront. Hair fall, thinning hair and scalp health are key concerns, with Minimalist and South Korean brand Aromatica showing up as trending haircare brands. Iso Beauty highlights interest in haircare solutions that deliver salon-quality results at home, while &Honey underscores the popularity of Japanese hair care brands with formulations inspired by honey-based ingredients catering to consumers seeking hydration, shine, and frizz control. Meanwhile, Wow Skin Science reflects continued demand for plant-based haircare products.

On TikTok, #BadNailsCheck has users showing manicure disasters, sharing nail art that turned out completely different from the reference photo. In contrast, #DamagedHairSolutions signals users on a “healthy hair journey”, sharing tips, routines, and product recommendations for repairing damaged hair. #DIYBlush reflects the growing appeal of personalized beauty, with creators customizing blush shades. #MotherOfTheBrideMakeup highlights demand for elegant, age-inclusive makeup inspiration for weddings and other special occasions. Meanwhile, technicians and creators are sharing techniques, product recommendations, and behind-the-scenes glimpses of their daily work with #LashArtistOfTikTok.

Sources indicate that in the wellness space, there’s a growing interest in supplements and solutions that support long-term health, targeted nutrition, and proactive selfcare. Dopamine patches align with demand for wearable wellness solutions aimed at supporting focus, motivation, mood, and cognitive performance. The rise of menopause support supplements highlights interest in formulations that help manage hormonal changes, with consumers seeking products that address symptoms such as hot flashes, mood fluctuations, sleep quality, and overall wellbeing.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, kimchi supplements mirror continued focus on gut health, as more consumers look for probiotic-rich alternatives inspired by fermented foods to support digestion and microbiome balance. Vitamin B5 supplements lean into essential nutrients that aid the breakdown of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins, while supporting skin and heart health. Finally, longevity supplements satisfy a growing focus on healthy aging, with consumers seeking science-backed ingredients and formulations that support cellular health and vitality as part of a preventive approach to wellness.

When it comes to wellness brands, those spanning targeted delivery formats, science-backed nutrition, and performance-focused solutions are performing the best. Gentle Patch reflects demand for convenient, wearable wellness solutions, while Bioschwartz and Webber Naturals represent continued interest in supplement brands that offer vitamins, minerals, probiotics, and herbal formulations for everyday health. Swolverine signals growing demand for performance nutrition that supports strength and recovery, while Zhou Nutrition reflects interest in holistic supplements that promote energy, immune health, sleep, and healthy aging.

On TikTok, the #SummerGlowMakeup and #BeautyFavs hashtags reflect growing interest in curated beauty routines and product discovery, with consumers seeking seasonal makeup inspiration alongside trusted product recommendations. #GeodeNails lean into a demand for artistic, statement-making nail designs that emphasize creativity and self-expression. #DIYMicroLocsJourney adopts a personal storytelling format, as consumers document their hair journeys, while learning protective hair styling techniques. Meanwhile, #DollarTreeSkincareHaul spotlights affordable skincare products, as consumers explore budget-friendly options that fit into their selfcare routines.

In the bodycare category, there’s growing interest in products that combine targeted treatments, ingredient-focused formulations, and at-home wellness solutions. The rise in searches for cellulite oil suggests that consumers are seeking botanical oil blends and firming formulations designed for massaging into the skin as part of anti-cellulite routines. Grape soap highlights demand for playful, fruit-inspired products that combine functionality with novelty and aesthetic appeal. Meanwhile, the popularity of AHA body lotions signals continued interest in ingredient-led skincare, with consumers seeking exfoliating body creams that improve skin texture and smoothness. Epsom salt lotion and red light therapy panels reflect the growing adoption of at-home recovery and wellness routines, as consumers seek products and devices that support muscle comfort, recovery, skin rejuvenation, and temporary pain relief.

Science-backed brands with plant-based ingredients and luxury positionings are soaring. Hada Labo, a Japanese brand, and QV Skincare reflect continued demand for gentle, hydration-focused products that support healthy skin through barrier-supportive formulations. Just Nutritive signals a consumer preference for handcrafted, botanical-based products that emphasize naturally derived ingredients, while Nordic Goddess points to the growing intersection of wellness and bodycare, as more consumers seek topical solutions that incorporate THC and CBD for targeted relief. Meanwhile, La Mer underscores demand for premium bodycare, combining intensive hydration with a luxurious, sensorial experience.

Industry observers note that over on TikTok, #CheetahHair, #HaircutTutorials, and #HairFoils are all trending, reflecting a broader shift toward more experimental and technique-driven approaches to hair styling. #CheetahHair highlights bold, pattern-led hair looks that emphasize self-expression and visual impact, #HaircutTutorials points to the growing demand for accessible, step-by-step education from hair stylists, while #HairFoils underscores continued interest in professional coloring techniques. In addition, #PlaitsBraids highlights the appeal of finished braided styles, with content featuring both at-home and salon-created results for men and women. Meanwhile, #CoconutOilForSkin signals an ongoing interest in multi-purpose ingredients used across selfcare routines. Together, these trends reflect a move toward both skill-based hair experimentation and ingredient-driven selfcare practices.

Sources indicate that luxury fragrances are becoming more than a special occasion spritz. Consumers are investing in scents that have wide appeal, from sport fragrances for energy, freshness, and an active lifestyle, to sweet smells that have a touch of nostalgia.

In a recent development, tomato perfume underscores the rise of unconventional fragrance notes, reflecting curiosity around earthy and garden-fresh scent experiences that stand apart from traditional or gourmand offerings. Meanwhile, perfume-making kits are becoming increasingly popular, as rising interest in personalization and creativity push consumers to explore DIY fragrance creation and craft scents tailored to their individual preferences.

Sources indicate that riiffs and Assaf, both Arabian fragrance houses, reflect growing consumer demand for accessible fragrances with strong, long-lasting effects and scent profiles that blend Middle Eastern perfumery traditions with modern styles. Pure Instinct and Rahasya signal interest in fragrances that feel more personal and body-driven, where consumers are drawn to scents designed to interact with individual chemistry and enhance perceived personal appeal. Lore reflects demand for more experiential and concept-led fragrances, as consumers increasingly seek scents that go beyond smell to evoke places, moods, and narratives. Meanwhile, Miu Miu highlights the enduring influence of fashion houses within the fragrance category, as consumers continue to seek scents that blend luxury, creativity, and modern self-expression.

In a recent development, #RedDyedHair, #LashDye, and #SelfTannerHack all reflect a broader shift toward at-home beauty experimentation through DIY techniques. #RedDyedHair highlights bold self-applied color changes as a form of personal expression and transformation. #LashDye reflects interest in low-maintenance beauty routines, where people tint lashes for longer-lasting definition, and #SelfTannerHack indicates how shared tips are used to achieve more controlled, even tanning results. Then, #NosePatches and #NeckSkincareRoutine point to growing demand for targeted skincare solutions, with the former focusing on pore care and blackheads for a quick, temporary smoothing effect, while the latter underscores increasing awareness of often-neglected areas that require attention beyond the face. Together, these trends reflect a move into DIY-driven beauty and targeted treatment routines.

When it comes to nails, consumers are seeking designs that blend self-expression, practicality, and care. BB cream nails reflect demand for natural-looking, low-maintenance manicures, while comic nails highlight a desire for creative and expressive nail art. Matcha nails point to the growing traction of soft green tones, influenced by the cult popularity of the beverage, while solid gel nail glue indicates interest in durable, mess-free nail application, as consumers increasingly value long-lasting performance. Crystal nail files reflect a growing awareness of nail health, with consumers seeking gentler tools that help maintain strong, smooth nails and minimize damage.

In a recent development, the rise of The Gelbottle, Nail Reformation, Kleo Kolor, and Curvlife each proves growing demand for long-lasting nail solutions that deliver salon-quality results. The Gelbottle reflects interest in professional-grade systems that strengthen and enhance natural nails, while Nail Reformation and Kleo Kolor point to the popularity of reusable press-ons and durable at-home manicure options. Curvlife emphasizes ease of application through reusable soft gel press-ons and adhesive solutions that don’t require UV light. Meanwhile, Hermès underscores the premiumization of the nail category, with consumers seeking luxury nail products and tools featuring shades inspired by Hermès’s design heritage and silk draping — finished with a high-gloss, satin sheen in a single coat.

On TikTok, #CyberPunkNails reflects interest in futuristic nail art that combines punk influences, neon accents, metallic finishes, and bold 3D details. #SkinTintStick highlights demand for hybrid complexion products that offer light coverage with skincare benefits in a portable format. #TCAPeel and #MicrobiomeSkincare signal growing consumer interest in understanding the mechanisms behind skin behavior, from chemical exfoliation and skin renewal to the role of the microbiome in barrier health. In the case of #TCAPeel, viral social media content often emphasizes the risks of extreme at-home use. #HairLossJourney extends this same behavior pattern into haircare, where individuals actively seek to understand the causes of hair loss, sharing progress and seeking support and solutions. Together, these trends reflect a shift toward beauty that combines experimentation, care, and awareness of underlying skin and hair health.

It has been revealed that makeup products and techniques that deliver precision, convenience, and natural-looking results are soaring. Contour stain reflects demand for long-wearing, transfer-resistant sculpting products that provide definition with minimal maintenance throughout the day. Meanwhile, cool-toned blush and cool-toned contour underscore consumers’ increasing focus on shade accuracy. At the same time, ghost and pre-glued lashes highlight demand for effortless lash enhancement, combining natural-looking results with faster and easier application methods. Together, these trends suggest that makeup is evolving toward personalized routines that prioritize subtle enhancement, ease of use, and products tailored to individual features and preferences.

Across makeup brands, the rise of Elroel and Purito highlights the continued influence of K-beauty. Elroel reflects growing demand for adaptive complexion products that simplify shade matching, while purito emphasizes lightweight coverage and minimal formulations to avoid skin sensitivities. Dermatologist-founded Rodan and Fields further reinforces interest in hybrid complexion products that combine cosmetic performance with skincare benefits. Meanwhile, the popularity of Brow Daddy highlights consumers’ focus on expertly defined brows and professional-grade beauty solutions offering precision and long-lasting results. KJH.Brand, rolled out by makeup artist Katie Jane Hughes, underscores the appeal of creative, multi-use makeup that encourages self-expression and flexible application across the eyes, lips, and cheeks.

As more consumers focus on maintaining hair health and reducing damage, #BedtimeHaircare is trending on TikTok and reflects growing interest in overnight prevention treatments. #CollagenFilm highlights K-beauty innovation in the form of dissolvable collagen films, designed for topical application to deliver instant hydration and a smoother, firmer appearance. #BrowFreeze, meanwhile, reflects continued interest in lifted, feathered brow styling that creates a laminated look. #613AmazonWig signals demand for affordable, pre-lightened platinum blonde wigs that enable bold color experimentation without chemical processing, while #GluelessClosureInstall reflects a broader shift in wig culture toward accessible, low-damage styling, where consumers seek dramatic transformations that are easy to apply, comfortable to wear, and avoid the long-term commitment or potential damage associated with traditional installation methods. Together, these trends reflect a move to beauty routines that balance care and transformation, combining preventative habits with low-damage styling and skin-focused innovation.

In a recent development, consumers are on the hunt for science-led skincare innovations. Interest in silicone scar sticks reflects demand for effective scar products that support skin recovery and improve the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles, while simplifying daily treatment routines. Rising interest in needle patches highlights demand for advanced delivery technologies, which enable active ingredients to be delivered directly for enhanced efficacy and targeted results. PDRN creams and serums tap into regenerative ingredients, as consumers seek formulas associated with skin repair, recovery, and renewal. Meanwhile, growth in matte lip balms highlights a desire for hybrid lip products that bridge skincare and makeup, delivering hydration while providing both a tint and a matte finish.

Among trending skincare brands, Elm Biosciences underscores the rise in science-backed, clinically developed skincare, with a lab-to-patient approach focused on supporting long-term skin health and healthy aging. Wow Skin Science reflects demand for nature-inspired skincare, offering plant-powered formulations free from harsh chemicals. Sincerely Yours highlights the rise of dermatologist-developed skincare tailored to younger consumers, with a focus on barrier support and the unique needs of teenage skin. Isispharma represents the continued strength of dermocosmetic skincare, providing targeted solutions for concerns such as hyperpigmentation, rosacea, and acne through dermatologist-recommended formulations. Sunplay signals growing emphasis on daily sun protection, leveraging advanced Japanese skincare technology to deliver high-performance UV defense.

According to recent reports, on TikTok, #FireHair reflects growing interest in bold, high-impact hair color trends, as more consumers embrace expressive styles. #DyedLocsOnWomen highlights demand for dyed locs as a form of color expression across textured and protective hairstyles. #ShimmerLips leans into the continued interest in glossy, light-reflecting lip finishes, while #WrinkleTreatments underscores rising focus on preventive and corrective skincare solutions, as consumers seek ways to address aging. #HDFrontalWigs showcases high-definition lace frontal wigs, with content centered on installations and styling.

Sources indicate that in the haircare space, consumers are searching for products that combine active ingredients, scalp support, and at-home technology. Amino acid shampoos and Capixyl-based formulas reflect a demand for ingredient-led repair and solutions that strengthen hair, while addressing thinning and scalp health. Batana oil shampoos highlight an ongoing interest in nourishing botanical ingredients for hydration and scalpcare, while blonde hair masks emphasize maintenance of tone and softness in color-treated locks. At the same time, red light therapy hats signal the growing adoption of tech-enabled tools for scalp stimulation and hair growth.

According to recent reports, hairburst reflects a growing demand for haircare solutions that support stronger, longer hair and address thinning and breakage. KilgourMD represents a dermatologist-founded, science-backed approach to scalp health, offering a targeted system designed to treat hair thinning through plant-based prevention and care. Tgideas highlights interest in rosemary-based botanical haircare aimed at supporting growth, reducing breakage, and improving scalp health. Dr. Groot reflects the strength of Korean dermatological haircare that zeroes in on scalp balance and hair loss prevention through ingredients such as niacinamide, prebiotics, and probiotics. Trybello signals demand for haircare solutions designed to reduce hair loss and promote thicker, fuller-looking hair.

In a recent development, on TikTok, #HeatlessStyling reflects rising interest in low-damage hair routines, as consumers seek ways to achieve results without heat tools. #FastHairstyles highlights demand for quick, efficient styling solutions that slot into busy lifestyles while still delivering polished looks. #FaceGlitter signals continued engagement with expressive makeup, focused on bold, playful self-expression. #MonsterHighNails points to the rise of bold, character-inspired nail designs that emphasize individuality and playful aesthetics, especially among Gen Alpha consumers. #NailArtBrush points to the importance of precision tools in nail design, supporting detailed artwork and professional techniques, alongside guidance from nail techs on choosing the best brushes and how to use them effectively.

Consumers are increasingly drawn to wellness formats that blend supplementation, wearables, and at-home recovery tools into everyday routines. Pheromone gummies reflect growing interest in products that support confidence with a holistic appeal, while dopamine patches align with demand for wearable solutions aimed at focus, motivation, and cognitive performance. GLP-1 and NAD+ patches support metabolism, energy, and cellular function, and multi-collagen supplements continue to gain traction for beauty and structural benefits such as skin, hair, and joint health. Alongside these, percussive massage devices highlight the rise of accessible recovery technologies designed to reduce muscle tension and support circulation after exercise. Together, these trends reflect a shift toward personalized wellness routines using multiple formats that prioritize convenience and seamless integration into everyday life.

According to recent reports, javvy Coffee reflects growing demand for functional beverages that integrate wellness benefits such as supporting energy. Subtle, natural-looking makeup continues to be popularized by medium-coverage products such as concealers. In a recent development, #RushedMakeup shows that consumers are drawn to quick, ready-to-go routines that demonstrate how to look polished fast. #NailTechASMR reflects fascination with sensory content. #BeforeAndAfterFacelift signals that audiences are intrigued by dramatic visual transformations of cosmetic procedures. #SisterLockRetightening and #WigLaid highlights a strong interest in professional hair care expertise and the maintenance of intricate, high-effort hairstyles, while also capturing attention to precision and seamless style by showcasing how flawlessly wigs are styled and finished.

According to recent reports, the rise of scar sticks, PDRN serums, and liquid microneedling reflects a consumer increasingly invested in skin regeneration, barrier repair, and clinically backed ingredients. The portability and ease of scar sticks signal demand for convenient, targeted solutions, while liquid microneedling highlights appetite for professional-level collagen stimulation and enhanced absorption without in-clinic procedures. Industry observers note that trending skincare brands reflect a shift toward clinically grounded, barrier-focused skin health paired with sustainability and device-led innovation. Genabelle and Tosowoong, both K-beauty brands, exemplify this movement: Genabelle develops science-backed, microbiome and PDRN-driven formulas designed to repair the skin barrier, while Tosowoong targets brightening, anti-aging, acne, and dehydration. At the same time, the growing attention around Shark’s CryoGlow LED mask, targeting acne, fine lines and puffiness, reflects a desire for professional-grade treatments that accelerate results, reduce inflammation, and replicate clinic-grade procedures. Meanwhile, Bolt Beauty’s biodegradable single-dose capsules and Yepoda’s K-beauty-inspired active formulations underscore the rising ingredient literacy of consumers.
