Meanwhile, #NeonHairColor highlights bold experimentation and personal expression, while #GlowSunscreen reflects a skin-first mindset where protection and radiance are expected to work hand in hand. #ShadowLiner signals interest in detailed, technique-focused eye artistry, as creators break down application methods for more defined eye looks. #LipEssentials points to demand for streamlined, everyday lipcare that balances performance with convenience.

Recent findings suggest that the surge in beauty tools like red light therapy hats suggests that consumers are increasingly seeing the scalp as the biological foundation of hair quality, density, and longevity, embracing device-led, clinically inspired solutions they can use conveniently at home. Interest in ingredient-specific shampoo formulas featuring batana oil and amino acid, or those that are protein-free, reflects a more educated haircare buyer. Meanwhile, demand for hair smoothing serums points to a parallel desire for immediate polish and manageability. In a recent development, seapuri and Dr. Groot, both Korean brands, tap into the rising demand for scalp-focused, anti-hair loss care. Seapuri uses hydrating, mineral-rich formulas, including a water-based scalp serum to reduce hair loss and balance sebum, while Dr. Groot focuses on scalp-nourishing shampoos and targeted anti-hair loss solutions with a clinically inspired, results-driven approach. Hashtags like #SkincareRestock and #ShampooRoutine points to the importance of consistency and ritual. #StrawberryScents highlights an interest in nostalgic fragrance profiles, while #BasketballHairstyle reflects the influence of purpose‑driven, activity‑ready beauty content.

Consumers are getting creative thanks to the popularity of peel-off lip tints and liners. The rise of blue lip stain, which applies blue but reveals a pink or berry hue once peeled, speaks to the demand for color-shifting, pH-reactive formulas that feel personalized and surprising. Plumping lip liner reflects a desire for makeup that mimics cosmetic procedures, with consumers drawn to products that visibly enhance lip volume without injections. Meanwhile, plum mascara shows how consumers are exploring non-traditional but wearable color accents.

The top-growing makeup brands reveal a consumer shift toward inclusive design, minimalist aesthetics, as well as age and tool-specific solutions. Tilt Beauty reflects rising demand for accessible, user-friendly packaging and refillable formats that are sustainable. Sweed Beauty appeals to a growing audience seeking the no-makeup makeup look, through vegan formulations that deliver barely-there finishes for natural enhancement over heavy coverage. Meanwhile, Jung Saem Mool attracts those drawn to editorial-inspired, K-beauty artistry, and Prime Prometics caters to the needs of mature skin, emphasizing that makeup shoppers are increasingly seeking products that serve their specific life stage and texture needs.

According to recent reports, the rise of #HairExtensionsTutorial and #TakingOutBraids highlights that consumers are actively seeking step‑by‑step guidance for maintenance and technique. #FrenchHairPin and #PurpleHairDye underscore a growing appetite for aesthetic experimentation and trend‑inspired looks, where tools and color become playful ways to express personal style. Meanwhile, #UltaHairSalon points to the influence of in‑salon experiences and professional authority in shaping consumer choices, with users looking to bridge DIY learning and expert execution.

Industry observers note that skincare products that blend restorative care, gentle technology and everyday indulgence are on the rise. The popularity of scar sticks and PDRN serums points to the advancement in regenerative treatments that support healing and skin repair. Tools like ultrasonic skin scrubbers highlight consumers’ appetite for at‑home derm‑tech devices. It has been revealed that brands with ingredients-conscious efficacy, modernized wellness and at-home performance solutions are being sought after. Terra Lotus, powered by beef tallow-based care, signals a growing interest in animal-derived, nutrient-dense skincare rooted in traditional practices, as consumers seek richer, bioavailable alternatives to plant oils and lab-created moisturizers.

APLB and Genabelle continue to spike interest in science-backed K-beauty, especially products targeting hydration, brightening, and skin regeneration through actives like niacinamide and glutathione. Dermagist points to sustained interest in cosmeceutical-style anti-aging solutions. Finally, Shark Beauty’s expansion into skincare devices reflects the growing appeal of tech-enhanced and at-home treatments.

Industry observers note that consumers are eager to participate in viral beauty without overspending, as #AffordableLipOil and #AffordableMascara make strong cases for accessible versions of trendy, functional products. #ProfessionalHairProducts point to a growing appetite for salon-quality care. In contrast, #HydroDermabrasion reflects a rising interest for in-spa skincare treatments, as consumers turn to TikTok to understand the benefits of medical-grade exfoliation and glow-boosting facials. Meanwhile, #CranberryMakeup underscores the continued influence of seasonal and mood-based beauty aesthetics, as customers experiment with rich, warm tones to express personal style.

According to recent reports, exfoliating foot masks and hand masks are on a spike, as consumers approach the treatments with the same ritualistic care traditionally given to the face. Vegan body wash and magnesium body butter reflect a shift toward wellness‑aligned, ingredient‑conscious products. Meanwhile, exfoliating body lotion bridges treatment and care, showing the consumer’s need for multifunctional products that improve texture and moisture in a single step.

Brands like Dettol and Noshinku show that trusted hygiene and germ‑defense solutions remain top of mind. Recent findings suggest that these top‑growing TikTok beauty hashtags reveal a consumer mindset that values efficacy, personalization, real‑world practicality and community‑driven discovery. At the same time, #LazyGirlSkincare and #ThinHairTips reflect a demand for simple, low‑effort solutions that fit into busy lifestyles or specific concerns. Sources indicate that the surge in interest for marshmallow perfume and chocolate perfume reflects a continuous craving for gourmand, dessert‑inspired scents. The rise of rose vanilla perfume and bridal perfume suggests people are gravitating toward romantic and memory‑evoking fragrances. Growing searches for oil‑based perfume show an increased interest in long‑lasting and body‑centric scent formats, revealing a preference for fragrance that melds seamlessly with one’s natural scent and lasts longer than traditional sprays.

Matière Première takes on the farm‑to‑fragrance purity and minimalist luxury, with its raw material‑focused compositions. Sensitivity-aware routines, personal customization and ingredients‑led problem-solving beauty are growing hashtags on TikTok.

Finally, #CoffeeSkincare points to the ongoing appeal of natural, functional ingredients, as people are drawn to the antioxidant and circulation‑boosting benefits of coffee in skin and hair routines.

Bold nails are back and it’s all about self‑expression and textured innovation with growing interest in statement cheetah print designs rooted in nostalgia and glamour, blending animal prints with modern finishes and clever color shifts. It has been revealed that the popularity of #OilToFoamCleanser reflects growing interest in innovative hybrid formats, suggesting consumers are drawn to easy and elevated routines. #OilySkinHack points to a problem-solving mindset, where users seek shareable solutions tailored to specific skin concerns, especially shine and congestion. Meanwhile, #ManiInspo and #GlitterHighlighter showcase visual beauty through inspiration and self-expression, with consumers looking for aesthetic ideas that feel fresh, playful and mood-driven. Lastly, #EdgeControlFor4cHair emphasizes the demand for texture-specific solutions and culturally resonant beauty techniques.

Matte powder is trending, as consumers seek polished, smooth and filtered‑like skin finishes. The popularity of pink lip stain and lipstick pencil, meanwhile, highlights a tilt toward bold lip looks that are still accessible and day‑to‑day friendly. Techniques like tightline eyeliner illustrate how subtle definition is gaining traction, reflecting a preference for minimal effort with big impact. Contrastingly, the surge in black lip stains suggest that consumers are also embracing more daring, identity‑driven looks that go beyond enhancement.

Industry observers note that among the top‑growing makeup brands, there’s an emphasis on accessible, niche aesthetics and cultural authenticity across price points. Sources indicate that on beauty TikTok, trending hashtags reflect a consumer behavior shift toward accessibility, self‑expression and targeted problem‑solving. The surge in #EyelashLiftAndTint showcases how people are seeking out tutorial‑friendly content and at‑home techniques to achieve salon‑level transformations. Meanwhile, #BraidingExtensions and #NailsDesignIdeas point to a growing appetite for creative styling and personalization in hair and nails. Lastly, #PinkLipLiner reflects a subtle shift from cool-tone nudes toward warmer, reddish-pink tones that add soft color while still feeling natural — indicating consumers’ evolving preference for makeup that enhances without overpowering.

The rise of morning shed, the ritualized removal of multiple overnight beauty tools and treatments, highlights a growing fascination with stacked, intensive skincare routines that promise overnight results. Searches for face-lifting masks reflect a desire for visible tightening, while hydrogel’s jelly-like, cooling texture satisfies a craving for sensorial, soothing formats. Meanwhile, rising interest in milky toners and turmeric face creams shows demand for gentle nourishment and targeted actives, with turmeric specifically valued for its natural, hyperpigmentation-reducing benefits.

By brand, Grace & Stella and Byoma each represent a demand for approachable, feel-good skincare — whether through playful formats like eye masks or barrier-repair formulas that emphasize maintenance and simplicity. In contrast, brands like AnteAge, Bioeffect and Medik8 cater to a results-focused audience seeking science-led actives like EGF and retinal, signaling rising trust in clinical, regenerative skincare that targets aging and skin renewal at a deeper level. Consumers are embracing a dual approach to skincare, blending routine-friendly support with targeted, high-performance treatments, depending on need, mood, or life stage.

In the TikTok sphere, trending beauty hashtags are focusing on age inclusivity, professional-level prep, and tailored care for specific identities and beauty concerns. #BeautyOver60 spotlights content that speaks directly to mature audiences, as those aged 60-plus seek routines and products that speak to their evolving needs and celebrate aging confidently. #BridalSkinPrep, often used by makeup artists, reflects interest in expert-driven techniques that enhance makeup application, as consumers value the behind-the-scenes steps that create flawless, event-ready skin. Meanwhile, #CollegeHairstylist, #RedHaircare and #CeramideSerum point to highly specialized content — from on-campus hairstyling services to color-specific hair routines and barrier-supporting ingredients — illustrating a broader trend toward community-rooted expertise and ingredient-conscious skincare.

Haircare is of increasing importance to consumers, as beauty focuses go beyond the surface to tackle cosmetic concerns at their root. The rise of DHT blocker shampoos and scalp serums signal growing concern around hair thinning and scalp health, with consumers turning to targeted treatments that address hair loss at its source. Interest in lightweight conditioners and hair UV protection highlights desire for gentle hydration and environmental defense, which avoids build-up and leans into skincare. Hair fiber powders are also rising, especially among young males, as consumers seek quick-fix solutions to thinning and receding, issues becoming more prevalent in social dialogue.

It has been revealed that among haircare brands, there’s a consumer shift toward precision and wellness‑infused formulations. Cerave’s expansion into haircare underscores the demand for dermatologist‑approved, barrier‑support solutions — with ceramides and niacinamide anchoring formulas that consider scalp health as closely tied to hair health. Arey taps into a preventative and repigmentation‑focused niche by offering clinical systems to address greying hair, as more consumers seek anti‑aging hair solutions. Design Essentials and TGIN highlight a growing emphasis on texture‑specific haircare, delivering salon‑quality formulas for relaxed, natural and coily hair types. Meanwhile, Vichy brings its skin‑science heritage to hair with targeted treatments for dandruff.

According to recent reports, on beauty TikTok, trending hashtags reflect a consumer shift toward efficiency, targeted solutions and hacks. Fragrance notes like tonka bean, marshmallow and chocolate are doing the rounds this month, marking a shift towards gourmand scents that evoke warmth, nostalgia and emotional selfcare. In a recent development, in the burgeoning wellness space, there is a growing emphasis on emotional balance, stress management and functional optimisation. In the TikTok space, consumer mindsets are centring around practicality, inclusivity and education in beauty routines. #AcnecareRoutine and #3StepSkincare highlight a growing demand for straightforward, step-based regimes, especially those that are accessible and targeted towards specific skin concerns like acne. In contrast, hashtags like #FaceSteaming and #GlycolicPads reflect a focus on contemporary skincare and selfcare practices that emphasise health and rejuvenation. The rise of #SkincareAdventCalendar underscores the appeal of curated, discovery-driven experiences, where consumers can explore fresh products in a fun and engaging way.

Industry observers note that the top-growing skincare trends reflect a consumer focus on plant-based formulas and solutions that promise targeted results. Microneedle pimple patches, an innovation from regular pimple patches, offer deeper, more effective treatment for pimples and acne, while face taping taps into the desire for temporary anti-ageing effects by lifting and tightening the skin. Castor face oil, rice face masks and honey lip oil indicate a preference for nutrient-rich, plant-based remedies rooted in traditional beauty practices with hydrating and brightening properties. As for brands, Illiyoon and Beauty of Joseon underscore the influence of K-beauty, with a focus on calming, plant-based ingredients rooted in tradition, whereas Byoma represents a rising consumer focus on strengthening the skin’s barrier. YSL Beauty reveals that luxury skincare remains highly sought after, appealing to those who prioritise both efficacy and brand prestige. Overall, consumers are increasingly gravitating towards products that balance efficacy with gentleness, emphasising skin health and barrier repair.

Industry observers note that among this week’s trending TikTok hashtags, there is an apparent consumer interest in enhancing natural beauty via techniques and products that deliver noticeable, polished results. Hashtags such as #FullLipsTutorial and #VoluminousBlowout emphasise the desire for amplified, voluminous looks, while #NaturalHairHack shows a focus on embracing and enhancing natural hair textures. #BridalMakeupInspo reflects the importance of brands tapping into consumers’ life events. Meanwhile, #HydratingFoundation plays into the growing demand for makeup that not only enhances appearance, but also supports skin health through nourishing ingredients.

The rise in searches for scalp powders, pre-shampoos and scalp oiling indicates a growing consumer focus on scalp health and targeted care. Hair loss creams suggest that consumers are actively seeking solutions for hair thinning and plant-based treatments, with this trend overall reflecting an increasing preference for preemptive and restorative care routines whereby the scalp is considered an integral part of hair wellness. The top-growing haircare brands, like Hers and Act + Acre, highlight a consumer preference for clinically driven, treatment-focused products that prioritise hair health, particularly addressing concerns such as hair growth and scalpcare. Duke Cannon and Dr Squatch represent a shift towards grooming products often marketed to men that emphasise plant-based ingredients and rugged branding, while Gisou’s rise reflects the growing interest in products that care for the hair like hair oils and hair masks.

Overall, consumers are prioritising both preventative and recovery-oriented approaches in their haircare routines, with a noticeable lean toward multifunctional and plant-based remedies.

The rise in hashtags like #HyaluronicAcidFillers and #GrowthOilForHair indicates that consumers are deeply engaged with enhancing their appearances through clinical treatments and plant-based solutions. The popularity of #MensHairCutting highlights the increased attention to male grooming and personalised haircare trends, which is reflective of broader inclusivity across beauty content. Hashtags like #PamelaAndersonMakeup and #HalloweenLipGloss reveal a fascination with nostalgic and creative makeup looks, showcasing the playful and expressive side to beauty; however, Anderson’s no-makeup look is also driving growth for the hashtag.

The trending supplement category is being driven by holistic wellness, with an emphasis on immunity, gut health and stress management. Supplement ingredients like colostrum and active hexose correlated compound (AHCC) highlight increased interest in immune-boosting ingredients, while magnesium oil and bergamot reflect a shift towards plant-based stress and mood regulation. Notably, sea moss ties into the growing popularity of nutrient-dense supplements. As for brand standouts, Armra Colostrum and Legendairy Milk indicate rising interest in immune support and maternal health. XWerks and Bodyhealth, meanwhile, reflect the focus on performance optimisation, particularly in fitness and recovery. Codeage appeals to a desire for comprehensive wellness, offering multi-functional supplements. Overall, the search data indicates that consumers are seeking multifunctional solutions to address both physical and mental well-being.

According to recent reports, consumers are seeking practical, problem-solving beauty solutions that fit seamlessly into their everyday lives. Hashtags such as #EasyHairHacks and #MakeupForGlasses highlight a preference for accessible, quick tips that enhance personal styling. #AcneSpecialist and #UnderArmBotox reflect rising interest in targeted treatments, with the latter signalling a shift in facial procedures like Botox as they move to the body for broader application. Additionally, the #FrenchBeauty hashtag references consumers looking to global beauty ideals for inspiration.

The top-growing bodycare trends reveal a consumer focus on ingredient-driven skincare products that address specific needs. Ingredients like turmeric and glutathione reflect a growing demand for offerings that have brightening and antioxidant properties, appealing to those seeking a solution to hyperpigmentation. Meanwhile, bodycare brand CLN Wash, addresses the needs of acne-prone and sensitive skin, reflecting a growing awareness of the importance of gentle, effective cleansing options. Retinol hand cream highlights an increasing interest in anti-ageing solutions, particularly for areas like the hands, which are often overlooked in skincare routines. As for brand standouts, Luna Daily focuses on microbiome-balancing formulations for all skin types, including intimate areas, showcasing a holistic approach to skin health, while Cocoapink’s commitment to plant-based ingredients resonates with a demand for gentle products that promote overall skin health without harsh chemicals.

The fastest-rising beauty hashtags on TikTok reveal a dynamic shift in consumer preferences towards inclusive and personalised beauty experiences. #YellowBraids highlights a celebration of unique hairstyles and cultural expression, as well as a desire for individuality in beauty choices. The emergence of the #ManFacial signifies the increasing interest of male consumers in skincare and grooming. Meanwhile, hashtags such as #AcneProneMakeup and #GelMoisturiser underscore a growing focus on targeted solutions and textures for specific skin concerns. The #ScalpFacial hashtag ushers in the skinification of haircare, reflecting consumers’ desires for holistic approaches that prioritise both skin and hair health.

Industry observers note that the top-growing fragrance trends in search data reveal a strong consumer preference for gourmand and comforting scents like vanilla, caramel, and watermelon, indicating a desire for sensory indulgence and familiarity, as well as more subdued edible scents like matcha. The rise in interest in discovery sets suggests consumers are becoming more experimental, seeking variety and personalisation in their fragrance choices while the popularity of body mists, which are lighter and more versatile than perfumes, indicates consumers' interest in layering scents for everyday wear. Notable top-growing brands include By Rosie Jane Lattafa and Sabrina Carpenter’s Sweet Tooth fragrance brand highlighting the appeal of niche fragrances and celebrity-backed scents. Overall, consumers are drawn to personal storytelling and the emotional connection tied to specific brands or figures.

The top-growing beauty hashtags on TikTok this week suggest that consumers are seeking seasonal and therapeutic beauty experiences. Hashtags like #skincareadventcalendar and #falllippie highlight the appeal of season-specific products and rituals that tie beauty to key moments or holidays. #Skincaretherapy and #promakeuptip emphasise a desire for expert-driven tips and routines and the rise of #frecklemakeup demonstrates how consumers are embracing creative self-expression through makeup trends.

According to recent reports, nail concealers and nail growth serums are among the main drivers for consumer interest within the nail space, reflecting the desire for both healthy nails and restorative care. Bow nails and green chrome nails, meanwhile, highlight the growing appeal of playful, bold nail designs as a means of personal expression. As for the category’s top-growing nail colours, Spate indicates pastel colours (+52.5 per cent year-on-year) and sheer finishes (+26.6 per cent year-on-year). Overall, these trends suggest that consumers are seeking a balance between nail care and artistic self-expression, blending practicality with creativity.

It has been revealed that the popularity of #GoingOutMakeupLook and #NoMakeupMakeupRoutine indicates that consumers are seeking bold, glam looks for social outings, alongside more subtle, natural styles for everyday wear; reflecting versatility in beauty preferences once again. #BlushTok remains strong as a trend that enhances consumer’s natural features using playful and exaggerated blush techniques. Elsewhere, #ItchyScalp is on the rise, signalling an increased consumer attention to scalp health, while #StraightBackBraids points to a growing interest in protective hairstyles that celebrate cultural identity and practical hair care.

The top makeup trends suggest that consumers are increasingly prioritising long-lasting products in their beauty routines, as well as opting for products that allow for the creation of bold makeup looks. Tubing mascara and brow stain highlight a desire for smudge-proof, day-long wear, while duochrome eyeshadow and cluster lashes reflect an interest in multidimensional looks that stand out. Brands like Mob Beauty, Gressa and Tower 28 Beauty emphasise the demand for plant-based, skin-friendly formulations that appeal to consumers who value health-conscious beauty routines. Meanwhile, Devinah Cosmetics and Lethal Cosmetics cater to those seeking bold, artistic expression through vibrant, high-pigment colours and hues.

When it comes to makeup concerns, there is a strong consumer focus on achieving a clear, smooth complexion while avoiding issues that could exacerbate various skin problems. Concerns about sebum and comedogenic products highlight a widespread desire to manage oil production and prevent clogged pores, indicating a need for non-irritating and breathable formulas. The focus on cakey makeup suggests that consumers are zooming in on how product texture and application impact the natural appearance of their skin.

Overall, these trends underscore a consumer inclination towards high-performance, visually impactful products that enhance and define key features.

Recent findings suggest that the growing interest in these skincare trends reflects a consumer shift towards plant-based formulas and DIY beauty routines. Consumers are increasingly drawn to ingredients with perceived holistic benefits, such as rice, honey and turmeric, indicating a preference for products that promise gentle and effective results. The emphasis on hydration, seen in trends like water-based cleansers, highlights a desire for clean, non-greasy solutions that maintain skin balance. Additionally, the rise of face taping suggests a growing interest in non-invasive techniques for achieving youthful skin and prioritising prevention.

The rising popularity of these skincare brands reflects a consumer preference for specialised, ingredient-focused products that cater to specific skin needs. Consumers are gravitating towards brands that emphasise science-backed formulations, as seen in Sebamed’s focus on pH balance and Byoma’s barrier-boosting ingredients. There’s also a growing appreciation for multicultural influences, with brands like Illiyoon and Sabbatical Beauty drawing from Korean skincare traditions, and Elaluz offering formulas with Brazilian superfoods.

The increasing focus on skincare concerns indicates a consumer shift towards addressing specific, often sensitive, skin complications. Consumers are becoming more aware of the underlying causes of skin problems, such as the impact of pore-clogging (comedogenic) ingredients and the influence of skin conditions like eczema and fungal acne. This trend suggests a growing demand for targeted treatments that are gentle, effective, and suitable for delicate areas like the eyelids. Additionally, the rise in searches for chin acne can be linked to lifestyle factors, such as mask-wearing and stress, as well as hormonal factors, driving consumers to seek solutions for these rising concerns.

Industry observers note that consumers are increasingly focused on scalp health and hair strength, as evidenced by the rising interest in scalp oiling and scalp serums. The popularity of hair loss topical solutions and rosemary shampoo reflects a preference for products that not only combat hair loss but also nourish and fortify the hair. The growing interest in low-porosity shampoo indicates a heightened awareness of individual hair needs and a desire for personalised care. Overall, these trends suggest a prioritisation in holistic haircare routines that enhance both scalp health and hair resilience.

The top-growing haircare brands reflect a consumer shift towards products that prioritise formulations and solutions. Brands such as Seen, Gisou, and Act + Acre are gaining traction for their emphasis on scalp and hair health, highlighting a holistic approach to beauty that starts with the skin and scalp. Dr Squatch, meanwhile, underscores a demand for plant-based products that are often associated with masculine grooming. Pattern Beauty’s growth signals a focus on inclusivity and products tailored to specific hair types and curl patterns. Overall, these trends indicate a consumer preference for personalised and ingredient-driven haircare solutions.

Among the trending haircare ingredients lies a consumer preference for multi-functional components that offer both therapeutic and cosmetic benefits. Ingredients such as wild ginger, rosemary and eucalyptus reflect a demand for plant-based products that promote scalp health, stimulate hair growth and enhance overall hair vitality. The rising interest in jojoba highlights a trend towards deeply moisturising and nourishing formulas. The inclusion of ketoconazole, an antifungal agent, indicates that consumers are increasingly interested in more targeted treatments, particularly for conditions like dandruff or other fungal-related concerns. Overall, these trends suggest that consumers are gravitating towards ingredient-driven haircare solutions that blend traditional remedies with contemporary benefits.

The rise in active hexose correlated compound (AHCC) and rutin supplements indicates a focus on niche, immune-boosting and antioxidant-rich ingredients, while the demand for melatonin-free sleep aids suggests a shift towards non-hormonal alternatives for enhancing sleep, partly driven by concerns over long-term supplement use. Tower pilates are reflective of the trend towards low-impact yet effective exercise routines. Increased searches for magnesium oil highlight a preference for topical and targeted approaches to stress and muscle relaxation, aligning with the broader trend of holistic, multi-benefit wellness products.

The trending wellness and supplement brands underscore a shift towards specialised wellness products that offer personalised benefits, resonating with consumers who are increasingly informed and selective in their wellness choices. XWERKS and Bodybio’s popularity also highlights a demand for performance-focused and bioavailable products, catering to consumers seeking optimal health and athletic performance. Bioray’s rise can be partly credited to a trend towards detoxification, aligning with a broader desire for holistic wellness solutions.

The rising search interest in ingredients such as colostrum and sea moss suggests a growing consumer focus on nutrient-dense supplements that support immune health and overall well-being. AHCC and rutin highlight ingredients that cater to targeted health concerns, such as immune system support and antioxidant benefits. Meanwhile, the popularity of L-theanine indicates a desire for stress relief and cognitive support through plant-based, non-stimulant solutions.

The search data for current bodycare trends reveals a consumer shift towards a ‘skinification’ of bodycare products, like turmeric soap and retinol hand cream, indicating a desire for comprehensive solutions that address specific concerns such as hyperpigmentation and anti-ageing. Interest in tallow soap, meanwhile, reflects a preference for hydrating and nourishing ingredients, whereas the popularity of peach body wash and vanilla body scrub underscores the importance of combining functionality, like cleansing and exfoliation, with pleasurable, aromatic experiences. Consumers are revealing an increased preference for both heritage brands and product innovation in personal care. Native’s rise showcases a trend towards affordable products that prioritise simplicity and effectiveness, and Saltair’s popularity indicates a growing interest in bodycare that incorporates active skincare ingredients and botanicals, blending nourishment with an elevated experience.

Sources indicate that ingredients addressing specific skin concerns while indulging in self-care are emerging. Turmeric’s popularity highlights a focus on targeting hyperpigmentation, while tallow reflects a growing demand for holistic ingredients that offer moisture and hydration. Peach and Tahitian vanilla suggest a desire for ingredients that combine skin benefits with indulgent and aromatic experiences. Sandalwood’s appeal points to an interest in soothing scents that enhance a holistic approach to bodycare.

Industry observers note that fragrance trends with the greatest prominence across search data all highlight a desire for convenient and versatile scent experiences. Meanwhile, oil-based perfumes and hair fragrances indicate a demand for long-lasting and multifunctional products that integrate seamlessly into daily routines, like fragrance layering, for example. The heightened interest in travel perfumes reinforces the need for portable and convenient products that cater to the on-the-go lifestyles of beauty consumers.

Sources indicate that among the top-growing fragrance brands in search data, there is a clear consumer preference for both classic brands and more contemporary lines crafted by celebrities. Consumer behaviour in the fragrance sector reflects a strong preference for refreshing and exotic scents. The growing interest in matcha and watermelon highlights a trend towards unique, invigorating notes that evoke freshness, while the popularity of gourmand scents suggests a desire for rich, indulgent fragrances that offer a sensory experience reminiscent of delicious treats. The rise of fruity notes like pineapple and lemon refer to a long-standing preference for bright and uplifting scents.

Consumers are increasingly focused on innovative nail products and enhancing nail health and strength. On the other hand, there is also growing interest in nail growth serums, reflecting a desire for products that enhance nail health and strength. Alas, the resurgence of 2000s nails and the rise of blue chrome nails indicate a growing interest in nostalgic and bold aesthetic expressions. Overall, these trends suggest that consumers are prioritising nail care routines that combine convenience, precision, and personal expression.

According to recent reports, the top-growing nail brands in search data reflect a significant consumer shift towards eco-friendly and non-toxic products, highlighting consumers’ knowledge regarding nail product formulas and ingredients. The top-growing nail colours and prints in search data reflect a consumer preference for both bold and understated aesthetics, indicating a desire for versatility in personal style. In a recent development, the top-growing makeup trends in search data reveal a consumer preference for long-lasting and low-maintenance beauty solutions. Among the makeup brands trending in search data, there is a clear consumer inclination towards both innovative formulas and inclusive beauty offerings. The top-growing skincare trends in search data indicate a strong consumer preference for gentle, effective skincare solutions that prioritise balance and clarity. According to recent reports, the search data also reflects a consumer shift towards innovative and science-backed beauty solutions. In a recent development, skin concerns like saggy and dehydrated skin highlight a demand for products and facial services that address specific skin issues such as loss of elasticity and moisture retention, respectively. The search for non-toxic products underscores a broader trend towards ingredients consumers perceive as safe, reflecting a growing awareness for skincare that supports overall skin health and avoids potential harmful effects.

As seen in the rising interest in scalp oiling and hair loss topical solutions, consumers are increasingly focused on scalp health and hair strength. The popularity of hair strengthening shampoos and rosemary shampoo highlights a preference for products that not only cleanse but also fortify and nourish the hair. While the interest in low porosity shampoo indicates a growing awareness of individual hair needs and a desire for customised solutions. The top haircare brands in search data reveal that consumers prioritise both luxury and specialised solutions for their haircare needs. The rising popularity of ingredients like wild ginger, rosehip and rosemary suggests a focus on health and wellness, as these components are known for their nourishing and therapeutic properties. Recent findings suggest that the top wellness and supplements trends reveal consumers are engaging in a multifaceted approach to health. The popularity of detox supplements and sea moss supplements indicates a growing focus on internal cleansing and nutrient-rich products, especially reflected in the rise in searches for magnesium oil, which suggests an increasing awareness of mineral supplementation for stress relief and muscle recovery.

Recent findings suggest that the top-growing wellness and supplement ingredients in search indicate a wider trend towards targeted nutrition. The popularity of black cohosh reflects a desire for herbal-based solutions that combat hormonal and menopausal symptoms. Industry observers note that bodycare trends highlight a consumer shift towards holistic and innovative self-care practices. The growing popularity of peach body wash reflects a consumer preference for bodycare products that offer both pleasant sensory experiences and nourishing ingredients. The interest in specialised products, such as boob masks and body cleansing oils, indicates a growing focus on comprehensive and targeted skincare routines. In a recent development, the rising interest in bodycare brands such as Caudalie and L’Occitane indicates a growing consumer preference for premium and specialised personal care products. Consumers are increasingly seeking out brands that offer a luxurious experience and prestige marketing, as evidenced by the popularity of these brands. The focus on targeted solutions, such as those offered by Summer’s Eve for feminine hygiene and Cln Wash for dermatological needs, suggests a demand for products that address specific concerns. It has been revealed that consumers are gravitating towards products and ingredients that combine sensory pleasure with functional efficacy in their bodycare routines. Ingredients such as sandalwood and turmeric indicate a preference for traditional and holistic remedies known for healing properties and targeted efficacious results. The popularity of Tahitian vanilla and peach highlights a trend towards fragrant ingredients that enhance feeling of bliss and tallow reflects an interest in rich, moisturising substances that provide deep nourishment. Together, feeling and function pave way for the category.

Recent findings suggest that experimentation and personalisation usher in a upcoming era of scent exploration. The year-on-year growth for discovery sets, pheromone perfumes, and oil-based and roll-on scents suggest consumers are seeking variety as well as the ability to sample before committing to a full-size purchase. Discovery sets are averaging at 1,600 monthly searches, which reflects a strong desire for value and exploration in scent choices. As sample-size scents witness positive growth, fragrance variety in the form of roll-on and oil-based products follow closely behind in a shift towards long-lasting and portable fragrance solutions that appeal to convenience and a desire for subtle scent choices. As consumers seek variety, they are more receptive to experimenting with fragrances that enhance personal allure and attraction (for themselves and others). The rise in pheromone perfumes align with a consumer desire for products that boast confidence-boosting properties. Together, these trends highlight a consumer base increasingly interested in adaptable and sensory-enhancing fragrance options.

The fragrance brands turning heads are reflective of storytelling and innovation, spanning luxury, heritage and lifestyle appeal. Consumers’ fragrance preferences come alive in two worlds: one, familiarity and nostalgia brought about by musks and amber oils; then, fruity and tropical aromas. The search for classic musk and amber oils indicates a desire for comfort and warmth, while the rise of watermelon, pineapple and coconut signifies a craving for fresh and tropical notes that evoke experiences and locations. This suggests an openness to unique and bold fragrances, with a twist of nostalgia. The combination of traditionally masculine notes (musk and amber) and lighter, unisex options (fruits and coconut) reflects a move away from rigid gender norms in fragrance choices that continue to reflect the blossoming gender fluidity in scent.

Sources indicate that the top-growing nail trends reflect a consumer demand for innovative and efficient solutions within the nailcare space. Sophistication, individuality and creativity are among the key themes for nail colours and finishes. In a recent development, the rising search trends for silicone primer, tubing mascara, multichrome eyeshadow, cluster lashes and eyebrow stain indicate a consumer shift towards long-lasting, high-performance and customisable makeup products. These trends indicate a preference for innovative formulas — such as tubing mascara or silicone primer — that offer durability and ease of use. Multichrome eyeshadow and cluster lashes reflect a desire for expressive, bold looks with unique finishes. Meanwhile, the increasing interest in eyebrow stain points to a growing focus on low-maintenance beauty solutions that deliver semi-permanent results.

Growth across search for products that tackle textured skin, foundation transfer, eyebags, mature skin and comedogenic concerns indicate a consumer focus on achieving a flawless and long-lasting complexion. These concerns reveal an increasing demand for skincare and makeup solutions that address specific skin concerns, such as smoothing texture and preventing product transfer. The emphasis on eyebags and mature skin highlights a desire for benefit-driven options that cater to different life stages, while concerns around comedogenic products suggests consumers are increasingly clued-up on — and looking to avoid — formulations that clog pores and trigger breakouts.

The top-growing makeup brands — Typology, Tower 28 Beauty, Beauty Creations, Unleashia and Laura Geller — reflect a wider shift towards diverse, inclusive and innovative beauty solutions. These brands are known for their emphasis on skin-friendly ingredients (Typology and Tower 28 Beauty), as well as their playful and expressive cosmetic offerings (Beauty Creations and Unleashia). The popularity of Laura Geller reinforces the demand for products that cater to mature skin types via age-appropriate solutions. Overall, consumers are seeking brands that offer transparency, are tailored to various skin types and concerns, and strike the perfect balance between skincare and makeup.

Among the skincare trends gaining the most ground, there is a clear consumer preference for products that emphasise safety, effectiveness and innovation. Water-based SPFs and snail cream highlight a shift towards lightweight and hydrating formulations that cater to sensitive skin while offering multifunctional benefits. The interest in filler dissolvers and nano-infusion treatments reflects a demand for minimally invasive cosmetic procedures that provide quick and visible results. Kojic acid serum’s popularity underscores a desire for targeted solutions to hyperpigmentation, demonstrating a wider trend towards clearing and evening skin tone via potent active ingredients.

In a recent development, scientifically backed, versatile and natural ingredients are being prioritised by skincare consumers in their ingredient choices. Butylene glycol and propanediol indicate a demand for effective humectants that enhance moisture retention without causing irritation. Sulfur and kojic acid, meanwhile, focus on targeted treatments for acne and hyperpigmentation. The rise in searches for pomegranate oil points to a desire for natural antioxidants, emphasising the want for anti-ageing and skin-protective properties.

The top-growing skincare brands represent a blend of high-tech beauty tools, traditional and innovative skincare solutions, and luxury experiences. Illiyoon and Etude House signify a strong preference for K-beauty products — valued for their gentle, effective and often unique formulations. The rise of Byoma underscores a trend towards barrier-boosting, science-driven skincare, while YSL Beauty reflects a continued demand for luxury brands that combine skincare with sophisticated aesthetics and branding.

The top-growing hair colour trends suggest that consumers are gravitating towards subtle yet sophisticated shades that can be both natural and bold. Consumers are seeking creative expression and practicality in their hairstyle choices. Sources indicate that the growing search trends for supplements like manganese, PMDD, astaxanthin, AHCC and silica suggest a consumer shift towards personalised and condition-specific health solutions. There’s a clear increasing awareness and proactive approach to managing specific health challenges, such as hormonal imbalances, immune support and skin health. Consumers also prefer alternative, ‘natural’ remedies, as seen with interest in unique compounds like astaxanthin and AHCC. Brands should consider highlighting these ingredients or other components that look to target similar health concerns.

Recent findings suggest that top-growing selfcare brands like Vicks, Bragg, Optibac, Mommy’s Bliss and Qunol reflect a trend towards health-focused and preventative products. Vicks is a traditionally ‘medicinal’ brand that’s successfully venturing into supplementation as consumer interest in their ZzzQuil Pure Zzzs Melatonin Gummies continues to grow. Bragg and Optibac offer natural and probiotic options, including apple cider vinegar supplements and probiotics for women, respectively. Mommy’s Bliss caters to family health, particularly for infants and children, demonstrating an increased focus on safe and effective products for all family members.

Industry observers note that the rising popularity in searches for supplement ingredients suggests an increased focus on preventative health and functional benefits, with consumers seeking ingredients that support specific needs like cardiovascular health, cognitive function, hormonal balance and metabolism. Rutin, a bioflavonoid found in certain fruits and vegetables, is known for its antioxidant properties, its potential to reduce inflammation and, along with amino acid L-citrulline, the improvement of blood circulation. Meanwhile, L-theanine — an amino acid primarily found in tea leaves — is praised for its calming effects and ability to enhance cognitive function without causing drowsiness. These trends underscore a growing awareness and demand for natural ingredients that offer targeted health benefits, as well as a need to further the education around supplementation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you, like most people, hear the term “bourbon chicken” and have no idea what it is, let me call it by its more common name: toothpick chicken. Yes, the suspiciously delicious chicken shelled out at mall food courts on toothpicks is most likely bourbon chicken. Popular at American Chinese or Cajun-style Chinese restaurants, the sticky-sweet chicken is the utter definition of delicious, luring weary shoppers into food courts to find refuge from the bubblegum pink sweatpants and ripped denim. This version takes cues from the classic but swaps in some autumnal ingredients to make it fit for the season. Charred brussels sprouts leaves and pecans add bulk, while maple syrup and apple cider vinegar give it that delightful tart-sweet flavor we know and love. Serve it over rice or noodles or all by its lonesome for a hearty dinner that will take you back to the '90s.

More chicken dinner winners here: Sheet-Pan Hot Honey Chicken and Peaches; Basil Chicken Stir-Fry; and Ginger-Garlic Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry.

Recent findings suggest that whisk one 1½" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, ⅓ cup bourbon, ⅓ cup pure maple syrup, ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, ¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes, 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce, and ½ cup water in a small bowl to combine. Set sauce aside.

Toss 1½ lb. skinless, boneless chicken breasts, halved crosswise, thinly sliced against the grain, remaining 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, and remaining 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce in a medium bowl until chicken is coated; set aside.

Recent findings suggest that heat 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add 1 lb. brussels sprouts, halved through stems, leaves separated, and cook, stirring very occasionally, until just tender and blackened in spots, about 5 minutes. Transfer to another medium bowl.

Industry observers note that add more oil if pan looks dry and, working in batches if needed, arrange reserved chicken in a single layer and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Transfer to bowl with brussels sprouts.

In a recent development, add reserved sauce to same pan and bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened, about 1 minute. Remove pan from heat and return brussels sprouts and chicken to pan; top with 1 cup salted roasted pecans, coarsely chopped. Toss to coat in sauce. Serve chicken and brussels sprouts with steamed white rice if desired.

15 Best Zip-Up Hoodies for Men 2026, According to GQ Editors

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that surveying the best zip-up hoodies for men takes me back to my younger days as a hopelessly romantic high school kid.
  • In a recent development, gen-Z has revived every minute piece of 2000s pop culture, which means zip-up hoodies are back and have all but usurped the pullover hoodie as the sweat du jour.
  • Uniqlo’s no-nonsense clean aesthetic and low price point has made it a go-to for any menswear enjoyer looking for good style on a budget.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that surveying the best zip-up hoodies for men takes me back to my younger days as a hopelessly romantic high school kid. My formative years were marred by angst, soundtracked by pop punk, emo, and indie rock. The piece of clothing that got me through it all? A zip-up hoodie. It was core to the indie aesthetic, with every forlorn frontman sporting one over a thrashed band tee, skinny jeans, and shredded Chucks. But nostalgia never seems to stay in the past, especially when fashion is involved.

In a recent development, gen-Z has revived every minute piece of 2000s pop culture, which means zip-up hoodies are back and have all but usurped the pullover hoodie as the sweat du jour. The zip-up is inherently versatile in both practical wear and sheer styling dexterity. With the flick of the zip, you can put your beloved Death Cab for Cutie tee on full display while letting your pits breathe, or keep it zipped up when it's just a bit too nippy out. To find the best zip-up hoodies on the market, I dusted off Transatlanticism and went on a deep dive. The good news is that the old classics are still good. The better news is that there's a lot of great competition to choose from.

Uniqlo’s no-nonsense clean aesthetic and low price point has made it a go-to for any menswear enjoyer looking for good style on a budget. While the brand excels at cashmere sweaters, T-shirts, and a slew of homerun collabs, the Japanese label’s sweats are criminally underrated. We’d go so far as to say that they should be talked in the same breath as brands like Champion and Sunspel. This zip up hoodie took us by surprise thanks to its comfy midweight, all-cotton fabric and solid construction. But the main selling point is the impeccable fit.

So many other brands cut their hoodies too long in the body and leave you looking like Jack Skellington’s pubescent brother. Uniqlo managed to cut its French terry hoodie to sit right at the hips which makes for a more classic and natural silhouette that’s neither lanky nor sloppy. Because of the fabric, the feel, and the overall fit, this is my favorite zip-up hoodie by a sizable margin. It’s my most-worn hoodie and has yet to show signs of any fraying.

Industry observers note that hoodies were originally meant for sportswear, as warm up gear before a grueling game of football. These days, they’re more often worn for lounging on the couch to watch the kickoff. And if you want to kick it in comfort while saving your pennies for booze and amuse bouche for the major game with the boys, the best budget zip up hoodie to buy is Hanes’ EcoSmart zip hoodie. The fit is spot on—relaxed, but not sloppy, comfy in the body and the sleeves without swallowing you like a sand pit.

The fit is impressive for the price, and the overall quality means you’re getting a little more than what you pay for. It’s not a hoodie that’ll last you for too long, but it is a good quality piece for just 15 bucks. And when other hoodies offer lesser quality and worse-fitting options for about the same price? The answer is clear.

Industry observers note that it’s hard not to sing the praises of Reigning Champ, a brand that built its fleece empire on sweatpants and hoodies. The Canadian label’s flagship midweight terry fabric has drawn the attention of streetwear royalty and menswear buffs alike and its dedication to quality has elevated the humble hoodie to oxygen-deprived heights. We named Reigning Champ’s crewneck sweatshirt and pullover hoodie as among our favorites in their respective categories, and the same goes for its zip-up hooded sweatshirt. It’s made of the same 100% cotton French terry fabric as its superlative-earning brethren and is cut with high-quality flatlock stitching for a smooth, un-bulky feel.

I had high expectations for Reigning Champ, given my previous experience, and I’m not surprised at all with how nice this zip-up is. And while I'm partial to the standard fit, it’s also available in a slim fit version, too.

Hoodies live in a universe well beyond the sportswear world from which they originated. And while we still enjoy the OGs and the classics that made the hoodie a bona fide menswear must-have, we also love seeing all the ways the style has been pushed, tweaked, and freaked. Our Legacy's Level Hood has been a successful avenue for the Stockholm-based brand to explore the limits of the hoodie and this particular version strikes a delicate balance between the freaky and the fashion-curious. It's made of an English wool knit into an all-over ribbed texture for a throwback '90s feel. The cropped, boxy silhouette and elongated sleeves harken back to the grunge-y era, while the sultry dual-tone nightshade colorway throws you off in the best way possible.

It has been revealed that menswear influencers will be happy to regale you with their TedTalk on the golden ratio of clothing proportions. Essentially, that means your outfit should be divided into three equal sections where the top takes up one third of the outfit. Basically, your tops should be cropped and sit closer to your natural waist. Follow it up with some high-waisted pants with a wide silhouette and you’ve instantly garnered 300K views on TikTok (RIP). With so many indie brands and influencers scrambling to make their own versions of “the perfect cropped hoodie” you’re probably tired of wading through all the choices. Do yourself a favor and go to Abercrombie.

In a recent development, the Moose’s version is backed by actual trend forecasters, actual designers, and actual fit models. What does that mean, exactly? It means that its cropped zip hoodie fits really well and uses surprisingly beefy fabric. It was a revelation for me, too—Abercrombie wasn’t a name I associated with hoodies, but after I saw this in person, I had to readjust my menswear word cloud.

Industry observers note that some of the best zip-up hoodies for men are made by a brand you never see in brick and mortar stores. Camber has been crafting the most durable sweats for decades, right here in America and have been the shining example of the difference between good quality and great quality. Sure, you have to order through an old-school web 1.0 website and wait for several weeks to actually get your hoodie. But trust us when we say that the relatively minor inconvenience is completely worth it.

In a recent development, the heavyweight fleece is almost as thick as a leather jacket and can stand in as outerwear if you wanted it to. While other hoodies are washed to hell in giant industrial washing machines to reach a super soft texture by the time it gets to you, Camber’s actually require you to do the work yourself. It sort of feels like you’re being swaddled by an anaconda, which means if you’re a proponent of hard clothes like raw denim, you’ll like Camber’s hoodie a lot.

In a recent development, cashmere zip hoodies, once the exclusive province of Silicon Valley unicorn founders and PJ-flying nepo babies, have been democratized, none better than Naadam's take. You know the brand for bringing thoughtful, sustainable cashmere pieces at “really, only that much?” prices. Its zip hoodie is as soft as it gets, with extra credit points awarded for coming in a classic fit (too many cashmere hoodies err on the side of slim) and six colors, including this decidedly handsome olive. Wear it on weekends, work-from-home Fridays, and long flights—even if it's just Economy+.

It has been revealed that shoutout to brother in arms Louis Cheslaw, GQ Recs contributor, whose writing for the newsletter Magasin put us on to young brand Cease. From seed to sewing, it's beefy 20-ounce cotton is fully American-made. Assembling the fabric vertically means the hoodie will shorten up to a slightly cropped, oversized fit. Act fast if you want some of the less-boring colors—they move fast.

Recent findings suggest that we can’t deny Russell Athletic’s contributions to the hoodie space. And while its formula has changed over the years, the fresh hoodies are still pretty good for the price. The fabric is soft and lightweight, and it’s available in a rainbow of colorways. Plus, if you’re looking for a hoodie with a little more length, this is a great option.

In a recent development, bold graphics aren’t usually deemed classics, but Gap’s retro-leaning collegiate-style block logo has staying power almost as much as the Levi’s red tab. Add to that a wonderfully fluffy midweight fleece material and a tailored straight fit and you’ve got something you’ll see on moodboards for generations to come.

Champion’s Reverse Weave fabric is iconic for its nearly shrink-proof quality and almost unsettlingly rough exterior. Flip it to the inside and you’ve got a luxuriously brushed interior that’ll have you feeling like you’re melting into a cloud. Heads-up that pricing varies kinda wildly by size on Amazon.

The secondhand market is chock full of navy-blue hoodies that have been sun-faded and beaten down with time. They'll cost you just as much as this Mfpen version, but will also fall apart faster than you can zip 'em up.

Les Tien's dedication to all things sweats results in a catalog of luxurious fleece and terry cloth with a modern approach. Featuring high-end Cobrax hardware, RiRi zippers, raw-edge hems and sleeves, and a heavyweight brushed fleece, no detail is phoned in.

Recent findings suggest that the Real McCoy's is considered by many to be Americana repro wizards. This revival of an early 20th-Century hoodie is just one small piece of the brand's preservation prowess. It's made using beefy sinker-knit fleece, old-school Talon-style zippers, and vertical patch pockets.

A.Presse's chokehold on the menswear illuminati refuses to let up and it's pieces like this vintage-inspired hoodie that keep the pressure on. Based on very rare “after-hood parkas", this made-in-Japan hoodie features an idiosyncratic attached hood, super dense and lofty fleece, with artfully distressed details throughout.

Think of the zip-up as the pullover hoodie's elder brother, but with way more layering potential. In its most natural state, it can cuddle up to a matching set of sweatpants and a baggy tee with flair. (Top it off with a swanky necklace, crisp sneakers, and some stellar shades and you’re left with a fit on par with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander at his tunnel-trotting best.).

In a recent development, unzipped and left open, it can also take on the role of a picture frame ready to display your sickest graphic tee—much like the cardigan, another treasure of 2000s fashion. Or make like a mid-Aughts garage band ironically donning corporate attire and wear your zip-up over a dress shirt and baggy tailored trousers, a high-minded fashion move with a jolt of kooky Scandinavian cool.

Style is subjective, we know—that’s the fun of it. But we’re serious about helping our audience get dressed. Whether it’s the best white sneakers, the flyest affordable suits, or the need-to-know menswear drops of the week, GQ Recommends’ perspective is built on years of hands-on experience, an insider awareness of what’s in and what’s next, and a mission to find the best version of everything out there, at every price point.

Recent findings suggest that our staffers aren’t able to try on every single piece of clothing you read about on GQ.com (fashion moves fast these days), but we have an intimate knowledge of each brand’s strengths and know the hallmarks of quality clothing—from materials and sourcing, to craftsmanship, to sustainability efforts that aren’t just greenwashing. GQ Recommends heavily emphasizes our own editorial experience with those brands, how they make their clothes, and how those clothes have been reviewed by customers. Bottom line: GQ wouldn’t tell you to wear it if we wouldn’t.

We make every effort to cast as wide of a net as possible, with an eye on identifying the best options across three key categories: quality, fit, and price.

In a recent development, to kick off the process, we enlist the GQ Recommends braintrust to vote on our contenders. Some of the folks involved have worked in retail, slinging clothes to the masses; others have toiled for small-batch menswear labels; all spend way too much time thinking about what hangs in their closets.

Sources indicate that we lean on that collective experience to guide our search, culling a mix of household names, indie favorites, and the artisanal imprints on the bleeding-edge of the genre. Then we narrow down the assortment to the picks that scored the highest across quality, fit, and price.

Across the majority of our buying guides, our team boasts firsthand experience with the bulk of our selects, but a handful are totally new to us. So after several months of intense debate, we tally the votes, collate the anecdotal evidence, and emerge with a list of what we believe to be the absolute best of the category right now, from the tried-and-true stalwarts to the modern disruptors, the affordable beaters to the wildly expensive (but wildly worth-it) designer riffs.

It has been revealed that whatever your preferences, whatever your style, there's bound to be a superlative version on this list for you. (Read more about GQ's testing process here.).

I Tried Hash Browns From 5 Fast Food Chains—This Is The One I’d Wake Up Early For

💡 Key Takeaways
  • People across the country take breakfast very seriously—after all, many believe it's the most notable meal of the day.
  • According to recent reports, I tried hash browns from five different fast food chains to see which one serves up the best during the morning rush.
  • Sources indicate that this proved to be one of the tougher taste tests I've conducted during my time at Delish.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

People across the country take breakfast very seriously—after all, many believe it's the most notable meal of the day. When you're rushing to work, grabbing something on the go is often the easiest option. And nothing screams breakfast quite like a side of hash browns. When a diner isn't in the cards, a fast food chain can be just the ticket.

According to recent reports, I tried hash browns from five different fast food chains to see which one serves up the best during the morning rush. Of the chains I tried, only Dunkin' serves hash browns all day. Everywhere else, you'll need to order during breakfast hours, which vary by location.

Sources indicate that this proved to be one of the tougher taste tests I've conducted during my time at Delish. There were truly no terrible options, and some of the differences were pretty small. Here's how they stacked up.

Burger King's hash browns come in a handy carton filled with plenty of small, round crisps. They have a crunchy exterior and, honestly, are perfectly adequate. They're just up against some tough contenders. Of all the spuds I tried, these were the least memorable and had the least flavor, though nothing about them was off-putting.

In a recent development, taco Bell served the most substantial hash brown on this list—it was quite hefty. The exterior had a nice crispiness, but compared to its competitors, the inside was much mushier, and the whole thing was noticeably greasier. It's not something I could eat a lot of.

In a recent development, dunkin's hash browns, which are served all day (!), were a bit more divisive in the Delish office. Some people stood ten toes down for the zesty onion flavor, while others (myself included) found it more reminiscent of leftover grease on a stove. That remarked, the texture was great, and whether you love them or hate them, these had the boldest flavor and stood out from the rest of the pack.

According to recent reports, like Taco Bell, McDonald's offers a larger hash brown patty than the others on this list. The chain totally nails the crispy outer edges and boasts great potato flavor. You can really tell this is McDonald's because the taste is so similar to the chain's iconic fries. If you like those, you'll love its hash browns. However, because of the patty's size, the middle lost some of the structure and crispiness I was looking for.

In a surprise win, Chick-fil-A's hash browns came out on top. The bite-sized pieces are easy to grab on the go, and their small size gives each one the perfect mix of a crispy exterior and soft interior. The flavor is spot-on, with savory onion and pepper notes. Best of all, they weren't overly greasy.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • More quick dinners this way: Spicy Chicken Lettuce Wraps; Gochujang Chicken Stir-Fry; and Easy Fish Tacos With Spicy Sauce.
  • boneless Fresh York strip steak (1–1½" thick), cut into 1" pieces, 1 Tbsp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A traditional steak dinner can feel like too much for a weeknight: too expensive, too likely to trip the smoke alarm, too fussy to cook to a perfect medium-rare. But cut a steak into bite-size pieces and suddenly it transforms into a quick-cooking protein that’s no more demanding than chicken breast or tofu. Rub the steak with the spices and make the quick no-recipe yogurt sauce a few hours ahead if it’s helpful with time management. To account for the extra liquid thrown off by the spinach as it cooks, the water-to-couscous ratio in this recipe differs from that often found on the back of the bag (or box) so measure accordingly.

More quick dinners this way: Spicy Chicken Lettuce Wraps; Gochujang Chicken Stir-Fry; and Easy Fish Tacos With Spicy Sauce.

Place 1–1¼ lb. boneless Fresh York strip steak (1–1½" thick), cut into 1" pieces, 1 Tbsp. dried oregano, 2 tsp. onion powder, 2 tsp. sugar, and 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl; season generously with freshly ground pepper and toss to coat. Let sit at least 10 minutes or cover and chill up to 8 hours (no need to bring to room temperature before cooking if chilling).

According to recent reports, heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or medium Dutch oven with a tight-fitting lid over medium. Add 1 bunch scallions, thinly sliced, ½ cup finely chopped dill, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until scallions are softened, about 5 minutes. Add 10 oz. baby spinach in 2–3 handfuls, stirring and letting wilt slightly after each addition before adding more, 5–7 minutes total. Pour in 1 cup water and bring to a boil; season with more salt if needed. Add 1 cup Moroccan couscous and stir to break up any lumps. Remove from heat; swiftly cover with lid and let sit 10 minutes.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, heat 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet, preferably cast iron, over high. Arrange steak in a single layer; cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, 6–8 minutes. Reduce heat to medium; continue to cook, stirring often, until meat is just cooked through, about 1 minute more. Remove from heat. Add remaining 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; toss to combine. (Residual heat from pan will cook out any raw garlic flavor.).

Sources indicate that uncover couscous and fluff with a fork to separate grains. Spoon into a large shallow bowl or onto a platter. Top with steak. Cut 1 lemon into quarters and squeeze juice from 1 quarter over steak. Scatter thinly sliced cucumber and some dill sprigs on top; drizzle with oil.

In a recent development, combine 1 cup plain whole-milk yogurt and a generous pinch of kosher salt in a small bowl; squeeze juice from 2 lemon quarters into yogurt. Stir to combine. If sauce is thick, stir in water, a spoonful at a time, to loosen.

Serve steak and couscous with yogurt sauce and remaining lemon quarter and more lemon wedges for squeezing over.

#20241. Breaking: The 22 Best European Christmas Markets to Visit This Winter

📅 01 Dec 2022 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2380 w)
